# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Leaf-aware downtime dispatch (audit tier)

## Problem statement

The downtime worker requires ALL slots free (default `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots: 0`) before any dispatch, because a parent audit's Phase 2 fan-out (1 parent + up to 2 children) needs the whole pool. But most audit candidates are **leaf items** (no children) — their audit is a single Pi session needing **1 slot**. Requiring all slots free for a leaf audit wastes partial-idle capacity (e.g. 1 or 2 of 3 slots free) that could run it locally.

This is Q5 lever 2: make the audit tier check `wl show <id> --children --json` at selection time and require fewer free slots for leaf audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Audit-tier selection (`deps.getNextAuditCandidate` or `dispatchDowntimeWork`) fetches the candidate's children (`wl show <id> --children --json`; fail-closed → treat as parent, all-slots gate).
2. **Leaf candidate** (0 children): dispatch when at least 1 slot is free (`available_slots >= 1`) for the full idle threshold.
3. **Parent candidate** (>=1 children): unchanged — all slots free (with the bounded fan-out item, effectively 2 slots needed in cheap mode, 3 in fast).
4. Same-slot stability: the "same N slots free for the full threshold" guarantee requires per-slot identity — this item is BLOCKED BY LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA (proxy exposes `slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]` in `GET /llama/local/status`). Until it lands, leaf dispatch keeps the all-slots gate (no behavior change).
5. Optional (documented, not required): the race-accepting variant — dispatch on `available_slots >= 1` without per-slot identity, accepting that an interactive request may grab the slot and the audit's first call falls back to remote. Default OFF; fail-closed philosophy preserved.
6. Tests: leaf vs parent classification, children-query failure → parent gate, per-slot idle tracking integration (reuses WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG tracker), race-accepting variant toggle.
7. README documents the leaf/parent dispatch difference and the per-slot dependency.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked-by**: LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA (proxy per-slot details, llm worklog) — same enabler as WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG.
- **Related**: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (bounded audit fan-out — makes parent audits fit the pool, complementary); WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracker — the per-slot idle-duration machinery this item's gate consumes).
- **Related**: WL-0MSOMV6CW003OXTK (idle threshold 60s) — coordinate timing defaults.
data.title: Leaf-aware downtime dispatch: leaf audits dispatch on fewer free slots

## Refactor: decompose `src/sync.ts` god class

**File:** `src/sync.ts` (1,867 lines, 34 exports)

## Problem statement

`src/sync.ts` exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts decomposition). It concentrates
merge logic, author-identity validation, remote fetching, delta replay and
push operations in a single module, making navigation, review and safe
change harder than necessary.

## Users

- **Developer maintaining sync** — needs to locate and edit one concern without
  scrolling 1,800 lines. *As a maintainer, I want merge logic isolated from git
  plumbing so a merge fix does not require reading push code.*
- **Code reviewer** — needs a focused diff surface per concern.
  *As a reviewer, I want to review a change confined to one cohesive file.*
- **New contributor** — needs learnable module sizes.
  *As a newcomer, I want each sync concern to be a file I can read in one sitting.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure
   (barrel and extracted modules) has ≤ 1,000 lines, verified mechanically
   (e.g. `wc -l`) and recorded in the completion comment.
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable
   from `'../src/sync.js'` / `'./sync.js'` (barrel re-export); no consumer
   source file or test file changes its import path or assertions.
   Verified by `tsc` build plus an unchanged test suite.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass
   without modification. Any accidental behavioural delta must be reverted,
   not "fixed" in place.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in
   the module responsibility table below; verified by build plus an import-graph
   check (no module imports a module that imports it back).
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a
   top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
6. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes via the test skill, and
   `npm run build` succeeds.
7. **Documentation updated.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (or the sync section it
   links) describes the new module layout; code comments reflect moved code.

## Constraints

- Preserve the public API exactly — barrel re-export only, no consumer edits.
- No new dependencies, no behavioural changes, no renames of exported symbols.
- Follow the existing `src/sync/` sub-module pattern (`merge-utils.ts` already
  lives there) and the `sync-defaults.ts` / `sync-phase-timings.ts` precedent.
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `MergeOptions` from `'../sync.js'`; it may
  be re-pointed to the new types module (internal, not a consumer).
- Scope is decomposition only. Any behavioural improvement discovered is filed
  as a separate work item, not absorbed here.

## Existing state

- `src/sync.ts` — 1,867 lines, 34 exports (23 functions/consts + 11
  interfaces/types), no internal section markers; concerns are inferable from
  declaration order.
- Already extracted: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` (52 lines, merge primitives),
  `src/sync-defaults.ts`, `src/sync-phase-timings.ts`.
- 10 source files import from `sync.js`: `database.ts`, `github-sync.ts`,
  `api.ts`, `logging.ts`, `index.ts`, `commands/{sync,doctor,init,migrate,helpers}.ts`.
- 11 test files import from `sync.js` (`sync.test.ts`, `sync-whitelist.test.ts`,
  `sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `sync-worktree.test.ts`,
  `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
  `sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`, and others).
- Recent history touching the file: `f39b2463` (sync phase timings),
  `4eb0cc6b` (claim-hold guard), `09ac2db7` (audit downgrade guard) — the file
  is under active change, which raises merge-conflict risk during the refactor.

## Desired change — module plan (cycle-safe)

Extract along the existing cohesive concern groups; `src/sync.ts` becomes a thin
barrel. Est. line counts derive from the current file's declaration ranges.

| New file | Est. lines | Contents | Depends on |
|----------|-----------|----------|------------|
| `src/sync.ts` (barrel) | ~60 | Re-exports of every module below | all |
| `src/sync/types.ts` | ~100 | `GitTarget`, `SyncResult`, `MergeOptions`, `IncomingCommit`, `SyncAllowedAuthors`, `AuthorIdentityOptions`, `AuthorIdentityViolation`, `AuthorIdentityResult`, `DeltaReplayResult` | `../types.js` |
| `src/sync/git-exec.ts` | ~90 | `sanitizeGitEnv`, `gitExecAsync`, `execAsync`, `execGitCaptureStdout`, `escapeShellArg` | `../process-lifecycle.js` |
| `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` | ~80 | `isRegressionDefault`, `isValueRegression`, `isEmptyMeaningfulField`, `isTerminalStage`, `isAttributedDelete` | `types.ts`, `merge-utils.ts` |
| `src/sync/field-merge.ts` | ~600 | `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `mergeRemoteItem`, `indexItemsById` | `merge-predicates.ts`, `merge-utils.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/merge.ts` | ~30 | `mergeWorkItems` | `field-merge.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` | ~130 | `mergeComments`, `mergeAuditResults`, `mergeDependencyEdges` | `merge-utils.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` | ~70 | `isOwnProjectItemId`, `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` | `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/author-identity.ts` | ~200 | `normalizeEmail`, `isAllowAllAuthors`, `isEmailWhitelisted`, `getRemoteAuthorCommits`, `checkAuthorIdentity`, `buildIdentityRefusalMessage`, `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` | `git-exec.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/refs.ts` | ~110 | `getLastSyncedRefPath`, `readLastSyncedRef`, `writeLastSyncedRef`, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha`, `getRemoteTrackingRef`, `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` | `git-exec.ts` |
| `src/sync/repo-context.ts` | ~60 | `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `getRepoRelativePath` | `git-exec.ts` |
| `src/sync/worktree.ts` | ~140 | `removeWorktreeFiles`, `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`, `withTempWorktree` | `git-exec.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/remote.ts` | ~200 | `getRemoteDataFileContentWithRef`, `getRemoteDataFileContent`, `replayRemoteDeltaChain` | `worktree.ts`, `git-exec.ts`, `refs.ts`, `repo-context.ts`, `../jsonl.js` |
| `src/sync/push.ts` | ~170 | `gitPushDataFileToBranch`, `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` | `worktree.ts`, `remote.ts`, `git-exec.ts`, `repo-context.ts` |

The layering is strictly bottom-up (`types`/`git-exec` → predicates → merge →
remote/worktree → push → barrel), so no cycle is created. Note that
`mergeRemoteItem` must live in `field-merge.ts` (not `merge.ts`) to avoid a
`merge → field-merge → merge` cycle.

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts` — Reduced to a barrel re-export preserving all 34 exports.
- `src/sync/types.ts` — Shared sync types currently interleaved with logic.
- `src/sync/git-exec.ts` — Git invocation, env sanitisation, stdout capture.
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` — "is this a regression / a default" predicates.
- `src/sync/field-merge.ts` — Same- and different-timestamp field merge (largest extract).
- `src/sync/merge.ts` — Public merge entry point.
- `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` — Comment, audit-result and dependency-edge merge.
- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — Cross-project prefix filtering.
- `src/sync/author-identity.ts` — Author identity gate and whitelist logic.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Last-synced ref and remote-tracking ref helpers.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Data-file/repo-root resolution and assertion.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Temporary worktree lifecycle helpers.
- `src/sync/remote.ts` — Remote content fetch and delta-replay chain.
- `src/sync/push.ts` — Data-file push and force-push/rewrite.
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — Existing primitives; re-point `MergeOptions` import.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Document the new sync module layout.

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks**
- **Merge-logic interdependence** — `mergeSameTimestampItems` /
  `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` interlock with `mergeRemoteItem`; hence the
  explicit placement of `mergeRemoteItem` in `field-merge.ts`. Mitigation: keep
  the predicates in their own leaf module.
- **Test-coupling blast radius** — 11 test files import from `sync.js`; a
  single missing barrel re-export breaks them. Mitigation: mechanical export
  parity check (compare the exported symbol list before/after).
- **Concurrent-change conflicts** — `src/sync.ts` changed in the last three
  sync-related commits; a long-lived branch will conflict. Mitigation: land as
  a small number of sequential commits (types/git-exec first, then merge, then
  remote/push, then barrel), each building green.
- **Circular imports** — mitigated by the layered plan above and verified by
  build + import-graph check.
- **Scope creep** — the file contains known awkwardness (e.g. duplicated
  worktree/push preamble). Record opportunities as new work items; do not
  refactor logic here.
- **`_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef`** — a test-only export must survive the
  barrel unchanged; `tests/sync.test.ts` depends on it.

**Assumptions**
- Barrel re-export from `src/sync.ts` is the accepted compatibility mechanism
  (matches AC 2 in the seed brief and the existing `index.ts` pattern).
- Test files need no decomposition; only production source moves.
- Line targets are estimates; distribution may shift between
  `field-merge.ts` and `merge.ts` provided all files stay ≤ 1,000 lines.
- No performance or runtime-import-order change is expected.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — downtime-worker.ts is a god class (parent refactor
  series; this item is `discovered-from` it).
- **WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W** — Sync invalidation and cross-instance heartbeat
  (completed; prior work in this module).
- **WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ** — Assignee sync regression guard (completed; owner of
  the `isRegressionDefault` / `isEmptyMeaningfulField` semantics that move here).
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — Sync must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items
  (completed; touched merge paths).
- **WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF** — decompose `src/github-sync.ts` (sibling decomposition).
- **WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ** — decompose `src/commands/init.ts` (sibling decomposition).
- **WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1** — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (sibling decomposition).

## Related docs

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — SQLite/JSONL sync architecture; needs the new module map.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — sync behaviour reference (link target for the layout).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — relevant to `src/sync/worktree.ts` extraction.

## Appendix

- Q: How should the decomposition be structured? — Answer (repo analysis):
  Extract along the existing declaration-order concern groups into a layered,
  cycle-safe module set with a barrel re-export from `src/sync.ts`. Research:
  read all 1,867 lines' declaration ranges, the 11 test importers and 10 source
  importers; found no existing sync split beyond `merge-utils.ts`. Precedent:
  WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (same pattern for `downtime-worker.ts`).
- Q: Do test files need to change? — Answer (repo analysis): No. All 11 test
  files import from `'../src/sync.js'`, which survives as the barrel. Source:
  `rg -n "from '../src/sync.js'" tests/`.
- Q: Is `MergeOptions` a cycle risk via `merge-utils.ts`? — Answer (repo
  analysis): Yes, a type-only import from `'../sync.js'` would point at the
  barrel. Mitigation: move `MergeOptions` to `sync/types.ts` and re-point
  `merge-utils.ts` to `'./types.js'`. Source: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts:2`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF** – Refactor: decompose src/github-sync.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines) (open)
- **WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1** – Refactor: decompose packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines) (open)
- **WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ** – Refactor: decompose src/commands/init.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: adopted, appropriate, behaviour, break, ceiling (+61 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, appropriate, behaviour, break, change (+61 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: answered, behaviour, break, change, class (+54 more)

# Refactor: retire the legacy root `src/persistent-store.ts` fork

## Problem statement

`src/persistent-store.ts` is a 1,653-line legacy fork of the SQLite store. It is
**not on the production path**: the `wl` CLI talks to `SharedWorklogDatabase`
from `@worklog/shared`, which constructs the store in
`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`. The root copy survives only for a
development benchmark, two direct tests and one type import, so it adds a
1,653-line maintenance burden (two divergent forks to keep in step) without
serving users. Retiring it meets the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted
for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 by removing the file rather than decomposing a dead
copy.

## Users

- **Maintainers** — no longer keep two divergent store forks in step; one store
  is the source of truth.
- **Agents implementing work items** — no dead 1,653-line file to search
  through or accidentally edit.
- **Reviewers / producers** — diffs no longer land in an unused fork, and the
  store surface has one home.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the legacy root store deleted, so that a store change
  cannot silently land in the copy that never runs.
- As an agent, I want `FtsSearchResult`, `SqlitePersistentStore` and the
  binding helpers reachable from `@worklog/shared/persistent-store`, so that
  tests and benchmarks use the same store as production.
- As a reviewer, I want the WAL-bounding and binding-helper coverage to run
  against the production store, so that the tests protect real behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Legacy file removed.** `src/persistent-store.ts` is deleted. No source file
   in scope exceeds 1,000 lines (`wc -l` before/after recorded on the work
   item). The root build no longer emits `dist/persistent-store.js`.
2. **Consumers migrated.**
   - `src/database.ts` drops the unused `SqlitePersistentStore` /
     `FtsSearchResult` import (both symbols are currently imported but never
     used).
   - `src/commands/search.ts` imports the `FtsSearchResult` type from the
     shared package instead of `../persistent-store.js`.
   - `bench/wal-read-latency.ts` constructs the shared
     `SqlitePersistentStore`.
   - `tests/unit/wal-bounding.test.ts` and
     `tests/normalize-sqlite-bindings.test.ts` import the shared store and
     helper functions.
   - Only import paths change in those files; test descriptions, fixtures and
     assertions stay identical.
3. **Shared package exposes the store façade.** `packages/shared/package.json`
   gains a `./persistent-store` subpath export
   (`types: ./dist/persistent-store.d.ts`,
   `import: ./dist/persistent-store.js`) so consumers resolve
   `SqlitePersistentStore`, `FtsSearchResult`, `normalizeSqliteValue`,
   `normalizeSqliteBindings`, `unescapeText` and `parseAuditWaiver` from the
   canonical package path. This is forward-compatible with the planned
   `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` decomposition (WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU),
   which keeps the façade path.
4. **Behaviour unchanged.** Storage behaviour, pragmas, SQL and FTS semantics
   are identical — the shared `importData` performs the same transaction plus
   `wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)`, and the shared constructor accepts
   `new SqlitePersistentStore(dbPath)` (all extra parameters default). The
   binding helpers are byte-for-byte identical between the two forks (verified
   during intake).
5. **No new circular imports or runtime dependencies.** Only the
   `@worklog/shared/persistent-store` subpath entry is added; no new package.
6. **Builds.** `npm run build` (which runs `build:shared` then `tsc`) passes;
   `packages/shared/dist/persistent-store.js` is emitted and the root
   `dist/persistent-store.js` is gone.
7. **Tests.** `tests/unit/wal-bounding.test.ts`,
   `tests/normalize-sqlite-bindings.test.ts`,
   `tests/search-fallback.test.ts`, `tests/fts-search.test.ts`,
   `tests/database.test.ts` pass unchanged in assertions (import paths only in
   the two direct suites), and the full project test suite passes (run through
   the test skill, not ad-hoc commands).
8. **Documentation updated.** All references to `src/persistent-store.ts` are
   corrected or removed: `docs/dev/wal-checkpointing-investigation.md`
   (three references, including the "root CLI store" claim),
   `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`, and the comment in
   `tests/cli/create-dedup.test.ts`; code comments that name the file are
   fixed.
9. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Producer decision recorded.** No external consumers use the tooling
  directly; everything works through the CLI (producer, this session). This is
  the authority for removing the shipped `dist/persistent-store.js` deep-import
  path. If that assumption is ever revisited, it becomes a new work item.
- **Scope boundary.** Only the legacy root `src/persistent-store.ts` and the
  minimal consumer/export plumbing needed to delete it. The shared fork's
  decomposition is WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU and is **not** absorbed here; do not
  refactor or "improve" the shared store while migrating.
- **Migration is mechanical.** Change import paths and remove the dead import;
  do not edit test assertions, fixtures or the shared store's logic. Any
  behavioural gap discovered en route becomes a `discovered-from` work item.
- **Subpath export, not a new entry point.** Add the `./persistent-store`
  subpath to the existing shared package; do not change `main`, `types` or the
  `.` export.
- **Serialise with the shared-package refactors.**
  WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU and WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT also touch
  `packages/shared` and the `npm run build` / full-suite gate; run them one at
  a time (soft mutual exclusion, either order).
- **No repo-wide file-length lint.** The 1,000-line ceiling remains a review
  rule for the parent sweep, not a new CI gate.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `src/persistent-store.ts` — 1,653 lines, 6 exports: `SqlitePersistentStore`,
  `FtsSearchResult`, `normalizeSqliteValue`, `normalizeSqliteBindings`,
  `unescapeText`, `parseAuditWaiver`.
- **Production path (verified):** `wl` → `src/database.ts` (93-line thin
  subclass) → `SharedWorklogDatabase` (`@worklog/shared`) → shared
  `SqlitePersistentStore` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts:226`). Compiled
  `dist/database.js` has no reference to `./persistent-store`.
- **In-repo importers of the root file (the complete list):**
  - `src/database.ts` — imports `SqlitePersistentStore`, `FtsSearchResult`;
    **uses neither**.
  - `src/commands/search.ts` — type-only `FtsSearchResult`.
  - `bench/wal-read-latency.ts` — `SqlitePersistentStore`.
  - `tests/unit/wal-bounding.test.ts` (122 lines) — `SqlitePersistentStore`;
    uses `importData`, `getAllWorkItems`, `close` (all present on the shared
    store).
  - `tests/normalize-sqlite-bindings.test.ts` (433 lines) — the three
    binding/escape helpers.
- **Shared package export surface today:** `packages/shared/package.json`
  exposes `.`, `./types`, `./worklog-paths`, `./lease-release`,
  `./model-cooldown`, `./icons`, `./fields` — **no** `./persistent-store`.
  `packages/shared/src/database.ts` does not re-export `FtsSearchResult`.
  `packages/shared/dist/persistent-store.js` is built (gitignored `dist`).
- **Fork divergence (why this is a retire, not a unify):** the shared copy adds
  read-only open, `PersistentStoreServices`, the in-memory query cache,
  delta-sync watermarks, audit invalidation and `transactionImmediate`; the
  root copy has the same `parseAuditWaiver` / `auditWaiver` column but none of
  those. The shared copy is the production one.
- **Prior related attempt.** WL-0MQJK4UF0002OKUD ("Extract concerns from
  `SqlitePersistentStore`", completed) proposed
  `src/lib/sql-bindings.ts`, `src/lib/fts-search.ts` and
  `src/lib/schema-manager.ts`; none exist in the tree or in any branch history.
  It is precedent for the decomposition shape, and its rationale is now moot
  because the file should not exist at all.
- **Stale docs:** `docs/dev/wal-checkpointing-investigation.md` calls the root
  file the "root CLI store" and says both stores apply identical pragmas;
  `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` and one test comment also name it.

## Desired change

Delete the legacy root fork and point its few in-repo consumers at the shared
store:

# Refactor: decompose `src/commands/interview.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, 9 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`src/commands/interview.ts` carries the whole `wl interview` backend — clarifying-section
detection, Q/A parsing and lossless re-serialisation, the producer-review explanation
(LLM + structured fallback), LLM-assisted question extraction, the interactive walkthrough
loop, readline plumbing and Commander registration — in one 1,630-line module. It breaches
the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7, so navigating,
reviewing and safely changing any one concern means holding the whole file in view.

## Users

- **Agents implementing interview/LLM changes** — need one concern (e.g. the answer
  re-serialiser, or the extraction prompt) locatable by file search instead of by reading
  1,630 lines; a monolith inflates context cost and increases the chance of editing the
  wrong helper with a similar name (`cleanQuestion` vs `firstLine` vs `truncateBytes`).
- **Reviewers/auditors** — need a diff whose blast radius is legible from the touched
  module boundary.
- **Producers running `wl interview`** — benefit indirectly: behaviour-preserving
  decomposition lowers the regression risk of every future change to the command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent fixing a Q/A parsing defect, I want the parser and re-serialiser in one
  focused module, so that I can reason about round-trip losslessness without loading the
  LLM and Commander code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to state one responsibility, so that I can
  judge a diff against a single boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the `wl interview` command behaviour and the public module
  surface unchanged, so that no test, registry entry or documented flag needs reworking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `src/commands/interview.ts` and every file under `src/interview/` is
   ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 500). Evidence recorded in the work
   item as `wc -l` output for the module family.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** All 41 current exports of `src/commands/interview.ts`
   (2 section, 4 Q/A, 15 explanation, 11 extraction, 5 loop, 4 registration) plus the
   default `register` export remain importable from the unchanged specifier
   `src/commands/interview.js` with identical names, kinds and signatures; the barrel
   re-exports the full surface. `src/command-registry.ts`
   (`interview: () => import('./commands/interview.js')`) is untouched and needs no edit.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, regex, message, ordering or flag
   changes. Test assertions, fixtures, `describe` titles and mock targets are unmodified;
   the only mechanical test change permitted is the lockstep split of the oversized suite
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines): every resulting file is ≤ 1,000 lines,
   `describe` groups move verbatim and only import paths change. Test count is preserved
   (the split neither adds nor drops a test).
4. **No circular imports, one direction only.** Extracted modules import concrete siblings
   and `../lib/*`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`; **no** `src/interview/*` module imports
   the `src/commands/interview.ts` barrel. The dependency direction is
   `commands/interview.ts` → `interview/*`.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Every new module carries a one-line module doc comment
   naming its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments/work-item ids
   (`WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67`, `WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK`, `WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF`,
   `WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66`, `WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX`) move with their code.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build` (tsc, NodeNext, `rootDir: src`) is green and the
   full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (command/module map), `CLI.md` if any wording
   drifts, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
   (release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports only. No "while we're here" rewrites, no
  renames of public symbols, no regex or prompt-text edits. Any incidental improvement
  found en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Layout: mirror `src/doctor/`.** Helpers for a single command live in a top-level
  feature directory (`src/doctor/*` ← `src/commands/doctor.ts`); this item follows that
  established precedent with `src/interview/*`. The entry file stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving to `dist/commands/interview.js` under NodeNext (a directory-index barrel
  `interview/index.ts` would break that specifier).
- **No new dependencies.** Only existing imports (`../lib/llm.js`,
  `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../mutation-lock.js`, `../types.js`,
  `../cli-types.js`, `readline`) may be used by the extracted modules.
- **No behaviour-parity tooling in scope.** A repo-wide 1,000-line guard is a separate
  open item (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL, `discovered-from` the sweep); this item verifies the
  ceiling with `wc -l` evidence plus a small structural assertion (see Risks).
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

`src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, single default `register`, no
module-level mutable state (only `const` regexes/constants). Section map (current `dev`):

| Lines | Section | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| 1–70 | File doc comment + imports | — |
| 71–116 | Section markers (regexes, `INSERT_WRAPPER`) | — (all private) |
| 117–160 | Section extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` |
| 161–564 | Q/A parsing and re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` |
| 565–873 | Producer-review explanation | 15 (caps, context/deps types, prompt, render, fallback, LLM result) |
| 874–1052 | LLM-assisted question extraction | 11 (instruction, caps, prompt, parser, result, extract fns, section insert/merge) |
| 1053–1260 | Core interview loop | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` |
| 1261–1291 | Interactive input | — (`createPromptLoop` private) |
| 1292–1630 | Types + command registration | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) |

Consumers: exactly one production importer — `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import,
default export only) — and one test file, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines, 19
top-level `describe` blocks, no `vi.mock`, imports 11 named exports + default). No file in
`src/`, `packages/`, `scripts/` or `bench/` imports any other symbol from the module, and
no documentation references the file path.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `src/interview/`, leaving `src/commands/interview.ts` as the
command entry (registration + interactive plumbing) **and** the public barrel. Proposed map
(export attribution is exhaustive — every current export belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Exports moved | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/interview.ts` (entry + barrel) | Commander registration, `register` action flow, prompt loop, deps surface, re-export of the full public surface | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) + all re-exports | ~400 |
| `src/interview/section.ts` | Clarifying-section heading detection and extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` | ~95 |
| `src/interview/qa.ts` | Q/A parsing, answer-region computation and lossless re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` | ~400 |
| `src/interview/explanation.ts` | Producer-review explanation: evidence formatting, prompt, render, structured fallback, LLM call | 15 exports | ~310 |
| `src/interview/extraction.ts` | LLM-assisted question extraction plus canonical-section insert/merge | 11 exports | ~200 |
| `src/interview/loop.ts` | Interactive walkthrough: prompt/persist answers, outcome accounting | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` | ~220 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`commands/interview.ts` → {section, qa, explanation, extraction, loop} →
{`../lib/llm.js`, `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`} and
sibling modules only. `loop.ts` → `section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `extraction.ts`;
`extraction.ts` → `qa.ts`, `section.ts`. No module imports the entry barrel (AC4).

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `src/interview/` and extract `section.ts` + `qa.ts` (the pure,
   dependency-free parsing core). Blocks the rest.
2. **`explanation.ts`** — largest LLM cluster; independent of the loop.
3. **`extraction.ts`** — depends on `qa.ts`/`section.ts` for insert/merge helpers.
4. **`loop.ts`** — core walkthrough; depends on slices 1 and 3.
5. **Closeout** — thin the entry barrel (`src/commands/interview.ts`), lockstep split of
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`, module-map documentation, `wc -l` evidence, build +
   full suite.

Slices are ordered so slice 1 blocks the rest and each slice is independently move-only and
verifiable with the changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — becomes entry + barrel; loses ~1,200 lines, keeps `register`
- `src/interview/section.ts` — new (heading detection/extraction)
- `src/interview/qa.ts` — new (parse/rebuild)
- `src/interview/explanation.ts` — new (producer-review explanation)
- `src/interview/extraction.ts` — new (LLM extraction + section insert/merge)
- `src/interview/loop.ts` — new (interactive walkthrough)
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — split in lockstep into `tests/cli/interview/*.test.ts`
  (parsing/rebuild, loop + extraction, command integration, command `--llm`/progress,
  explanation), assertions verbatim
- `src/command-registry.ts` — read-only (specifier must keep resolving)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — command/module map note for the new `src/interview/` modules
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `CLI.md` — read-only
  unless wording names the module layout (it does not today; verify, do not churn)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Silent behaviour drift in the re-serialiser** (the lossless round-trip is the command's
  subtle core; regexes are shared between parsing and rebuild). *Mitigation:* extract
  `qa.ts` first with zero edits, keep the 19 existing `describe` groups untouched, and land
  each slice as a separate move-only commit so a regression is bisectable.
- **Barrel/ESM resolution break.** `src/commands/interview.ts` must keep existing so
  `dist/commands/interview.js` is emitted; a `interview/index.ts` barrel would silently
  break the lazy registry. *Mitigation:* AC2 + the `lazy-command-registry` and
  `entry-point-split` suites as the oracle.
- **Circular imports** if `loop.ts` or `extraction.ts` reach back into the entry for types
  or helpers. *Mitigation:* AC4 — modules import siblings and `../lib/*` only; shared types
  live with their owning module (`section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `loop.ts`).
- **Test-file split churn.** 19 `describe` groups currently share one module scope.
  *Mitigation:* move groups verbatim; add no shared helper unless two target files need the
  same fixture, and then only a mechanical extraction.
- **Regrowth repeats.** This sweep already has a "completed" decomposition that never
  landed (see Related work). *Mitigation within scope:* documented single-responsibility
  module headers; the repo-wide guard is WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (separate, low priority).
- **Scope creep risk.** The split invites opportunistic "while we're here" cleanups — a
  parser rewrite, prompt-tuning, a new `--flag`, splitting the 266-line `register` action
  into sub-commands. *Mitigation:* AC3 forbids logic edits; any such opportunity is filed
  as a separate item linked `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGXN80006V9P` rather than absorbed.
- **Review fatigue on a wide-but-shallow diff.** A move-only refactor touches many files
  for zero behavioural gain, which can invite under-review. *Mitigation:* one concern per
  commit/slice, `git diff --color-moved` for reviewers, and the unchanged suites as the
  behaviour oracle.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to a test file only
  when it is touched in lockstep with its module (sweep rule; identical to
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3).
- **Assumption:** the full 41-symbol public surface is retained in the barrel rather than
  trimmed to the 12 symbols tests import. Trimming would be a breaking change for any
  external plugin consumer and buys nothing here; the barrel re-export is ~10 lines.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable — `src/command-registry.ts`
  and the CLI help output must be byte-identical for `wl interview`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled; opportunities observed en route
  become separate `discovered-from` items.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep/directive: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer Q1 answered).
- WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — sibling from the same sweep (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`);
  source of the lockstep test-split rule reused in AC3 and the module-map layout pattern
  (entry façade + cohesive modules + explicit dependency direction).
- WL-0MULI1N1N0001WRD — "CLI: Explanation path & new options" (completed); introduced the
  `--no-llm`/`--json` modes and the producer-review explanation path extracted here. (The
  seed description labelled this item "Interview LLM fallback"; the title above is the
  accurate one — the LLM *extraction* fallback is WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF.)
- WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 ("Interview replay feature"), WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK ("r-i interview
  explanation does not state why an item needs producer review"), WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF
  ("interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback"), WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66
  ("Feedback in interview when running LLM"), WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX ("Interview LLM config
  schema") — all completed; provenance items for the behaviour implemented in this file,
  cited in its doc comments and moving with their code.
- WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA — "Interview LLM fallback integration" (completed); the integration
  work behind the extraction fallback path extracted here.
- WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL — proposed repo-wide file-size guard (`discovered-from` the sweep);
  the reason this item's ceiling check is manual plus a small structural assertion.
- WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1, WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ,
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW — companion god-class items from the same sweep (`init.ts`,
  `github-sync.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Repo precedent for layout: `src/doctor/*` helper modules consumed by
  `src/commands/doctor.ts`.

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted ACs, parent
directive) plus two completed sibling intakes from the same sweep answer every open choice,
and all decisions below are reversible at plan/implement time. Recorded for review.

- **Q: Where should the extracted modules live?**
  **Recommended and chosen: `src/interview/`, mirroring the existing `src/doctor/`
  precedent** (top-level feature directory consumed by one command module). The entry stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving under NodeNext.
  Alternatives considered: (b) flat siblings `src/commands/interview-*.ts` (works, but mixes
  six command-specific helpers into the already crowded flat `src/commands/` namespace);
  (c) a `src/commands/interview/index.ts` barrel (breaks the emitted
  `dist/commands/interview.js` specifier the lazy registry depends on).

- **Q: How granular should the split be?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** five extracted modules plus the entry (map above), one per
  existing section banner, each 95–400 lines — comfortably under the ceiling without
  inventing new boundaries mid-move.
  Alternatives considered: a two-way split (parsing vs everything else ≈ 470 / 1,150 lines —
  fails AC1); eight-plus micro-modules (churn without benefit).

- **Q: Keep the full 41-symbol barrel, or trim to the 12 symbols tests import?**
  **Recommended and chosen: keep the full surface.** The parent epic's "used symbols only"
  barrel decision (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Q2) applied to a module where unused symbols were
  genuinely internal; here every symbol is a documented part of this command module's
  surface and trimming risks breaking out-of-repo plugin imports for ~10 lines of saved
  barrel. Behaviour-parity is the priority (AC2).

- **Q: Split the oversized test suite in this item?**
  **Recommended and chosen: yes, mechanical lockstep split only.** `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`
  (1,696 lines) exceeds the same ceiling, and the parent sweep rule evaluates test files in
  lockstep with their module (identical to WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3). Assertions, fixtures and
  `describe` titles are unchanged; only file location and import paths move.

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard here?**
  **Recommended and chosen: no — out of scope.** A guard is repo-wide policy
  (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) affecting every sibling god-class item. This item records `wc -l`
  evidence and (optionally, if cheap) a structural assertion that the interview module
  family stays ≤ 1,000 lines; the repo-wide gate stays a separate item.
## Related work (automated report)

# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate the existing action bodies and helpers into sibling
  modules, adjust imports and registration wiring; do not refactor their logic,
  rename flags, or reword user-facing output.
- **Entry point is fixed.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` must remain the dynamic
  import target in `src/command-registry.ts`; the split happens *behind* that
  path.
- **CLI-agnostic logic stays put.** `src/doctor/*.ts` holds CLI-independent
  validation logic (`status-stage-check`, `dependency-check`, `file-paths-check`,
  `hook-upgrade`, `foreign-items-check`, `audit-gaps-check`, `parent-check`,
  `podcast-scripts-check`, `fix`). It is consumed as-is; this item does not
  restructure it.
- **Serial, tree-green landing.** Extract the smallest subcommands first and the
  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and
  passes the suite.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the doctor CLI contract, and no
  edits to the TUI or other commands.

## Existing state

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is 1,658 lines on today's `dev`. Inventory of logical
sections (line ranges from the current checkout):

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | File header + imports | 1–30 | 30 |
| 2 | `DAY_MS` constant | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | `formatCacheBytes` helper | 33–46 | 14 |
| 4 | `DoctorOptions` type | 47–50 | 4 |
| 5 | `PendingUpgradeState` + `detectPendingUpgrades` | 51–92 | 42 |
| 6 | `buildPendingUpgradeFinding` | 93–129 | 37 |
| 7 | `printPendingUpgradeNotice` | 130–151 | 22 |
| 8 | `PendingCacheState` + `detectPendingCacheState` | 152–196 | 45 |
| 9 | `printPendingCacheNotice` | 197–207 | 11 |
| 10 | `register()` prologue + root `doctor` command definition | 208–217 | 10 |
| 11 | `doctor upgrade` action | 218–418 | 201 |
| 12 | `doctor stage-sync` action | 420–549 | 130 |
| 13 | `doctor prune` action | 551–649 | 99 |
| 14 | `doctor cache` action | 651–715 | 65 |
| 15 | `doctor foreign-items` action | 717–838 | 122 |
| 16 | `doctor audit-gaps` action | 840–877 | 38 |
| 17 | `doctor dangling-parents` action | 879–948 | 70 |
| 18 | `doctor priority` action | 950–1036 | 87 |
| 19 | `doctor file-paths` action | 1038–1150 | 113 |
| 20 | `doctor migrate` action | 1152–1271 | 120 |
| 21 | Root `doctor` action (findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices) | 1273–1657 | 385 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Single consumer.** Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports the module
  (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`), and only for the default
  export. There is no cross-module use of helpers defined in the file, so
  extraction needs no public barrel beyond the unchanged default export.
- **Existing precedent for a nested sibling directory.** `src/sync.ts` (1,828
  lines, itself the subject of WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ) already sits beside a
  `src/sync/` directory (`src/sync/merge-utils.ts`), so `src/commands/doctor.ts`
  + `src/commands/doctor/` follows an established repository shape.
- **CLI layer vs validation layer.** `src/doctor/` modules are pure,
  `PluginContext`-free validators; the monolith's bulk is CLI registration and
  output rendering. The split therefore belongs in the command layer, not in
  `src/doctor/`.
- **Test surface to keep green (unmodified).** 18 existing doctor suites —
  `tests/doctor-{dependency-check,file-paths,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-check,hook-upgrade,podcast-scripts,retired-stage,status-stage}.test.ts`
  and `tests/cli/doctor-{audit-gaps,cache,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-push,foreign-items,priority,prune,stage-sync,upgrade-notice,upgrade}.test.ts`.
  Source: `ls tests/doctor-*.test.ts tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Reduce `src/commands/doctor.ts` to a thin registrar that wires the root
`doctor` command and delegates each subcommand to its own module under a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory. Starting decomposition (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/doctor.ts` | Registrar only: imports the per-subcommand registrars, registers the root `doctor` command definition, documents the module layout | ~120 |
| `src/commands/doctor/notices.ts` | Shared helpers: `DAY_MS`, `DoctorOptions`, `formatCacheBytes`, pending-upgrade detection/notice, pending-cache detection/notice | ~180 |
| `src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` | `doctor upgrade` (migrations + hook upgrade, dry-run/confirm) | ~205 |
| `src/commands/doctor/stage-sync.ts` | `doctor stage-sync` | ~135 |
| `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` | `doctor prune` | ~105 |
| `src/commands/doctor/cache.ts` | `doctor cache` | ~70 |
| `src/commands/doctor/foreign-items.ts` | `doctor foreign-items` | ~130 |
| `src/commands/doctor/audit-gaps.ts` | `doctor audit-gaps` | ~45 |
| `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` | `doctor dangling-parents` | ~75 |
| `src/commands/doctor/priority.ts` | `doctor priority` | ~95 |
| `src/commands/doctor/file-paths.ts` | `doctor file-paths` | ~120 |
| `src/commands/doctor/migrate.ts` | `doctor migrate` (JSONL → SQLite) | ~125 |
| `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` | Root `doctor` action: findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices | ~390 |
| `tests/doctor-line-count-guard.test.ts` | Additive guard: every doctor module ≤ 1,000 lines (repo convention keeps tests under `tests/`) | ~60 |

Each per-subcommand module exports a single `register<Sub>Command(...)` function
taking the narrow typed context, keeping the extracted action bodies
byte-for-byte faithful apart from their new signature and imports. The registrar
invokes them in the same order as the monolith so `wl doctor --help` output is
unchanged.

Implementation order (each step leaves the tree green): `cache` → `audit-gaps` →
`dangling-parents` → `priority` → `prune` → `file-paths` → `migrate` →
`foreign-items` → `stage-sync` → `upgrade` → root validation/`--fix` → guard
test + docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — reduce to a registrar; keep `export default register(ctx: PluginContext)`.
- `src/commands/doctor/notices.ts` — new; shared notice/formatting helpers moved from the monolith.
- `src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` — new; `doctor upgrade` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/stage-sync.ts` — new; `doctor stage-sync` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — new; `doctor prune` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/cache.ts` — new; `doctor cache` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/foreign-items.ts` — new; `doctor foreign-items` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/audit-gaps.ts` — new; `doctor audit-gaps` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — new; `doctor dangling-parents` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/priority.ts` — new; `doctor priority` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/file-paths.ts` — new; `doctor file-paths` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/migrate.ts` — new; `doctor migrate` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — new; root `doctor` action, findings aggregation and `--fix` prompt.
- `tests/doctor-line-count-guard.test.ts` — new; additive ≤1,000-line guard for the doctor module family (repo convention keeps test files under `tests/`).
- `src/command-registry.ts` — verify unchanged (dynamic import path stays `./commands/doctor.js`).
- `src/doctor/*.ts` — verify unchanged (CLI-agnostic validators, consumed as-is).
- `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`, `tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md` — verify doctor references remain accurate; add a module-layout note where a source-layout note already exists.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class* (parent refactor
  series; this item was created by its intake sweep). Producer decision Q1 → A
  is inherited: each oversized production file gets its own work item, evaluated
  and decomposed where appropriate.
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class
  (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Precedent for the AC pattern:
  unchanged public entry point, unmodified tests, per-module line ceiling, no
  cycles.
- **WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E** — *Refactor guard: downtime-worker split invariants*
  (completed). Precedent for the additive split-guard test adopted in AC6.
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** — *Refactor: decompose src/sync.ts god class* (open).
  Sibling item; `src/sync/` is the directory-shape precedent used here.
- **WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ** — *Refactor: decompose src/commands/init.ts god class*
  (open). Sibling item in the same `src/commands/` directory; shares the
  "registrar + per-subcommand modules" shape.
- **WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J** — *wl doctor prefix: rename the project prefix …*
  (open). A future doctor subcommand that will consume the new module pattern;
  it is **not** in scope here.
- **WL-0MUTVB271007YKJZ**, **WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G**, **WL-0MSALMLYK00604IA**,
  **WL-0MQPS28DW008QFL3** — completed doctor features whose tests form part of
  the unchanged regression gate.
- Documentation: `CLI.md` (doctor command reference), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
  (source layout references), `docs/migrations.md` (`doctor upgrade`/`migrate`
  guidance), `docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` (`doctor file-paths` guidance).

Automated report: `find-related` (`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGKH1770008MNU.md`)
matched the three sibling refactor items WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1
and WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, plus `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
`packages/herdr/README.md` and `CLI.md` as file matches.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Lost provenance / silent logic drift (medium).** Large block moves invite
  opportunistic edits. *Mitigation:* move-only rule (AC3), the unmodified doctor
  test suites as the behaviour gate, and a review that diffs each moved block
  against the original.
- **Registration-order or wiring regression (medium).** Commander renders
  subcommands in registration order, so running registrars in a different order
  reorders `wl doctor --help`, and a forgotten registrar silently drops a
  subcommand. *Mitigation:* AC3 plus a review that diffs root and per-subcommand
  `--help` output against the pre-refactor binary, and the unmodified CLI suites
  (which exercise every subcommand) as the wiring gate.
- **Import cycles through the registrar (low).** A module importing back from
  `src/commands/doctor.ts` would create a cycle. *Mitigation:* AC5 — modules
  import only concrete siblings; the registrar imports downward only.
- **Test-file temptation (low).** Rewriting the 18 doctor suites' import paths is
  the easy path but erases the behaviour-preservation signal. *Mitigation:* AC3
  makes unchanged tests a hard gate.
- **Guard-test scope creep (low).** A line-count guard test could grow into a
  repo-wide lint rule. *Mitigation:* AC6 scopes it to the doctor module family
  only; a repo-wide rule is recorded as a linked follow-up
  (SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD covers the skill-level check).
- **Assumption A1 — single task, not an epic.** The file has 11 naturally
  separated subcommands and no cross-cutting mutable state, and the largest
  extracted module is ~390 lines; a single `task` with a sequenced inner order
  matches the `database.ts` precedent (WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO) rather than the
  epic-per-module shape used for the 9,362-line `downtime-worker.ts`.
- **Assumption A2 — module home is `src/commands/doctor/`.** The extracted code
  is CLI registration and output rendering (needs `program`/`output`/`utils`),
  while `src/doctor/` is deliberately `PluginContext`-free validation logic. The
  `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/` pair establishes the nested-sibling-directory
  shape.
- **Assumption A3 — no producer answer required.** Every open decision here is
  resolvable by repository inspection or inherited from WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7
  decisions; no new scope or contract question is raised.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Restructuring `src/doctor/`, rewording doctor
  output, merging subcommands, and adding a repo-wide file-length lint rule are
  tempting and **out of scope**; each is recorded as a linked follow-up rather
  than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q0 (inherited scope) — Does the "no file > 1,000 lines" goal apply to this
file specifically, or should this item also decompose other oversized files?**

- **Answer (producer, 2026-10-20, via WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Q1 → A):** *"Create
  refactor work items for each of the other files. … If any file is >1000 lines
  it should be evaluated for refactoring and if appropriate a work item should
  be created."*
- Applied: this item is scoped to `src/commands/doctor.ts` only; siblings have
  their own items (WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, …), and
  SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD carries the skill-level check.
- Source: `wl show WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 --json` description, Appendix Q1.

**Q1 (consumer surface) — Does anything outside `src/commands/doctor.ts` import
symbols from it, i.e. must a compatibility barrel be preserved?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** no. Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports
  the module, and only as `import('./commands/doctor.js')` for the default
  export; no other file imports any helper from it. Preserving the default
  `register` export is therefore sufficient and no re-export barrel is needed.
  Research: `grep -rn "commands/doctor" src/`; `src/command-registry.ts:114`.
- Consequence: AC2 requires only the unchanged default export; internal modules
  may be imported directly by the registrar.

**Q2 (module home) — Should the extracted modules live in `src/doctor/` or a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** `src/commands/doctor/`. The bulk of the
  monolith is CLI registration and output rendering (it needs `program`,
  `output`, `utils`), whereas `src/doctor/` is deliberately
  `PluginContext`-free validation logic (`status-stage-check.ts`,
  `file-paths-check.ts`, …) consumed by the command layer. `src/sync.ts` beside
  `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` establishes the nested-sibling-directory shape.
  Research: `head src/doctor/*.ts` import sections; `ls src/sync/`.
- Consequence: recorded as Assumption A2 and in the Key Files list; `src/doctor/`
  stays untouched.

**Q3 (delivery shape) — One task or an epic decomposed into child items?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection + precedent):** one `task`. The file has 11
  naturally separated subcommands, no module-level mutable state to preserve,
  and the largest extracted module is ~390 lines. `database.ts` (2,584 lines) was
  decomposed as a single task (WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO); the epic-with-children shape
  was adopted for the 9,362-line `downtime-worker.ts` because each extraction
  there was a large, independently mergeable slice.
- Consequence: recorded as Assumption A1; implementation still lands in a
  sequenced, tree-green order (smallest subcommands first, root validation last).

**Q4 (verification of the line ceiling) — How is "no file > 1,000 lines" kept
true after this refactor, given there is no repo-wide file-length lint?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** an additive guard test in the doctor module
  family (AC6), mirroring `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` added by
  WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E. A repo-wide rule is out of scope and is covered by the
  SorraAgents follow-up SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD (evaluate >1,000-line files in the
  refactor skill).
- Consequence: AC6 added; guard test is additive only, so AC3's
  "no existing test modified" still holds.

**Q5 (current size drift) — The item was created against a 1,582-line file; the
file is 1,658 lines today. Does that change scope?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** no scope change. The section inventory above
  was recomputed from today's `dev`; the extra ~76 lines are inside the existing
  `upgrade` and root-validation action bodies, which are already in scope.
  Research: `wc -l src/commands/doctor.ts` → 1,658.

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".
data.title: vitest.config.ts: remove dead top-level singleFork key (vitest 4 ignores it)

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.
- At least one automated test or benchmark assertion encodes the measured
  improvement (or, where the outcome is a recorded finding, a documented
  baseline that a regression test can compare against).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (372 lines) builds a fresh `Command` per call,
  registers every entry of `builtInCommands` (~30 imports), creates a plugin
  context via `createPluginContext(program)`, wraps `ctx.utils.getDatabase` to
  track opened DBs, installs `preAction`/`postAction` hooks for diagnostics,
  then parses `['node','worklog',...args]`.
- Each call monkey-patches and restores `process.stdout.write`,
  `process.stderr.write`, `process.exit`, `console.log/error/warn/info`, and
  `process.argv`, and applies the `--worklog-dir` override via
  `applyWorklogDirOverrideFromArgv` before the plugin context is created.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` (585 lines) provides `execAsync` on top of
  `runInProcess`, plus seeding helpers used in `beforeEach` hooks.
- Attributed cost split (from seed measurements): ~72 ms with no DB work
  (`--help`), rising to ~196–257 ms once a command opens SQLite — i.e. the
  majority of the per-call cost is on the DB/config path, not commander setup
  alone. Confirming this split with a per-phase profile is the first AC.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — Harness under investigation; candidate site for
  context/command reuse or per-file DB reuse.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `execAsync` wrapper and seeding helpers; any
  caching must stay transparent to these call sites.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `createPluginContext` / `normalizeFieldsArgv`; if cost
  is config load or context construction.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `applyWorklogDirOverrideFromArgv` /
  `setWorklogDirOverride` global override, relevant to cross-call reuse safety.
- `src/database.ts` (or equivalent DB module) and migration/schema bootstrap —
  if DB open/migrate dominates the profile.
- `docs/dev/` — test-suite performance notes, if a documented baseline is
  added.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8** — *Reduce time to run tests* (parent discovery item,
  completed). Its plan listed this item as follow-up #2 after the suite went
  624 s → 427–547 s.
- **WL-0MVH47YF300087AQ** — *read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation)*
  (completed). Introduced/referenced `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` and the
  tmp-dir/`tsx` helpers; establishes precedent for measuring and asserting
  spawn-count reductions in CLI tests.
- **WL-0MLB6RMQ0095SKKE** — *Refactor slow CLI tests* (completed). Broad
  precedent: audit per-test timings, stub external work, consolidate fixtures.
  Its ACs are suite-wide (30% CLI-suite reduction, determinism) and it never
  attributes `runInProcess` per-call cost, so this item is the narrower
  follow-up rather than a duplicate — its fixture-consolidation approach is
  the prior art to build on.
- Duplicate check performed (intake, 2026-10-31): no completed item satisfies
  these acceptance criteria; the hits above are context/precedent, not
  duplicates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ~200 ms per-call figure is reproducible on a quiet host;
  CI/loaded-host timings vary, so any improvement claim must use a same-host
  before/after comparison (as the AC requires).
- **Risk (scope creep):** if profiling shows production startup cost, the fix
  belongs in `src/` and touches every CLI user — that must be a separate,
  explicitly scoped item rather than an in-harness workaround.
- **Risk (fidelity):** caching a `Command`/plugin context or a DB connection
  across calls can leak commander option state or `--worklog-dir` overrides
  between tests, producing order-dependent passes. Any reuse must be proven
  safe with tests that deliberately vary `--worklog-dir` and global options.
- **Risk (measurement noise):** vitest worker parallelism and slot contention
  distort wall-clock; use the canonical suite run via the test skill and
  compare medians, not single runs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Intake path:** auto-complete (no interview). The seed context supplied by
  WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 already contained a measured problem statement, a
  candidate set of remediations, and a re-scope condition, so the well-defined
  heuristic (clear headline + measurable ACs + implementation notes) applied.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of existing work?** — Answer (intake, repo + worklog
  search): no. `wl search` on "in-process CLI harness" and "runInProcess test
  timing" returned WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 (parent discovery item) and
  WL-0MVH47YF300087AQ (read-cache spawn reduction) as context only; neither
  satisfies these ACs. Source: `wl search ... --json`, 2026-10-31.
- **Q: What were the intake-time additions?** — Answer (intake): added the two
  standing ACs (documentation updated; full suite passes), an AC requiring the
  measured improvement to be encoded in a test/benchmark or documented
  baseline, verified Existing state / Key Files sections, Related work, and
  Risks & assumptions. Original seed ACs were preserved unchanged.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the implementer, not blocking intake):** whether the
  achievable saving is large enough to justify harness-level reuse versus
  re-scoping to a production `src/` change — to be answered by the profiling
  step (AC 1).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MLB6RMQ0095SKKE** – Refactor slow CLI tests (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, action, added, additions, aggregate (+252 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: action, added, aggregate, alone, already (+242 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: action, added, alone, already, answer (+225 more)

> **Note on the automated report below:** its file matches are low-precision
> (keyword-union over a long brief). The authoritative related-work list is
> the manual *Related work* section above; `WL-0MQP303A900780R0` (Pi TUI
> escape key) and `WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6` (unused import) are not related.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-31)

Four child features, delivered in test-first dependency order. Every child is a
vertical slice (bench/test code + harness change + docs/observability), so no
horizontal phasing is needed: the item is a Small/Medium investigation, and the
first child's measurement decides the branch the third child takes.

| # | Child | Type | Effort / Risk | Depends on | Covers parent AC |
|---|-------|------|---------------|-----------|------------------|
| 1 | **Profile and attribute in-process harness per-call cost** (WL-0MVVXFXM6007QZ2L) | task | S / Low | — | AC 1 |
| 2 | **Reuse-safety and harness-contract tests (test-first)** (WL-0MVVXG0EQ0068WQB) | task | S / Medium | 1 | AC 2 (safety net) |
| 3 | **Reduce in-process harness per-call overhead (or record re-scope)** (WL-0MVVXG4B200968BF) | task | M / Medium | 1, 2 | AC 2, AC 3 |
| 4 | **Budget guard and consolidated docs for harness cost** (WL-0MVVXG3UW00250V5) | task | S / Low | 3 | AC 4, AC 5, AC 6, AC 7 |

### Design decisions recorded at planning time

- **Measurement before reuse.** Child 1 is a bench script
  (`bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`, modelled on `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`),
  not a test: it produces the attribution table and the
  harness-side-vs-production-startup verdict, which is this item's own stated
  first AC and the gate for child 3.
- **Test-first ordering.** Child 2 lands the fidelity/order/restoration tests
  plus a red-first "reuse actually happens" contract assertion
  (`getInprocHarnessStats()` counters) before any reuse is implemented.
- **Decision gate inside child 3.** If the profile shows the dominant cost is
  production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan), child 3 does not
  add an in-harness workaround: it records the finding, creates a
  `discovered-from` `src/`-scoped item, and closes with a documented baseline —
  which is parent AC 3 rather than parent AC 2.
- **Gate modelled on existing prior art.** Child 4 reuses the
  `bench/startup-import-budget.json` + guard-test pattern (CPU-time gate, wall
  normalised by a same-run bare-node control, clamped host-load factor) instead
  of inventing a new flake-prone timing assertion.
- **Measurement policy.** Numbers come from the bench script (child 1/3) and
  from canonical-suite runs through the test skill (`/skill:test`); no ad-hoc
  `vitest`/`npm test` invocations by agents.

### Plan changelog

- 2026-10-31: Initial decomposition — 4 children created in test-first order
  with blocking edges 1→2, 1→3, 2→3, 3→4; parent ACs mapped above; effort/risk
  re-estimated from the child WBS (Small / Medium, expected 11.75 h,
  recommended 20.75 h, range 14.5–30.0 h, confidence 75 %).
- 2026-10-31: Automated review stage 1/2 (requirements + completeness) moved
  the parent AC restatements into dedicated child ACs so AC coverage is
  machine-verifiable (coverage review now reports 100 %); no requirement was
  added or changed.

### Plan-phase questions & answers

- **Q: Is a production interview needed for this item?** — Answer (plan skill,
  2026-10-31): no. The intake path already established the measured problem
  statement, the candidate remediations, the re-scope condition, Key Files and
  the fidelity/measurement risks; the only open question (harness-side vs
  production-startup saving) is explicitly answered by measurement (child 1),
  so asking the producer would be a blocking question with a cheaper
  empirical answer. Source: this item's description, `## Existing state`,
  `## Risks & assumptions`, and the recorded effort/risk report comment
  (WL-C0MVVOWAYD004O7RI).
- **Q: Should the harness reuse work be gated behind the profile, or planned
  unconditionally?** — Answer (plan skill): gated. Parent AC 3 requires
  recording and re-scoping when the cost is production startup, and the
  fidelity risk means reuse must be justified by attribution plus
  characterisation tests. Encoded as the decision gate in child 3 and the
  red-first contract test in child 2.
- **Q: Which child measured the before/after suite numbers?** — Answer (plan
  skill): child 3 produces the per-call before/after from the profiler; child 4
  owns the canonical-suite before/after (median of ≥ 2 runs via the test
  skill), because the suite-level claim is only meaningful once the change and
  the guard are in place.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for child 1's implementer):** whether the achievable saving
  is large enough to justify harness-level reuse at all. Answered by the
  attribution table; if the harness share is small, child 3 takes the
  production-startup branch and the saving claim moves to the new `src/` item.

## Problem statement

in `vitest.config.ts` (pool `'forks'`, `isolate: true`). The dev host has 16
cores. WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 reduced per-spawn cost ~5× (bundle-based CLI
spawning) and cut the wall clock 30–35 % at matched load, but wall clock
remains dominated by the longest single files on the critical path
(`sync-vs-mutation` ~151 s, `close-recursive` ~121 s, `issue-management`
~88 s, `read-cache-spawn-reduction` ~84 s).

The brief explicitly listed parallelisation as out of scope ("record as
linked follow-up work items, not this brief") — hence this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measure the canonical suite at `maxWorkers` 4 vs 6 vs 8 on a 16-core host
  (median of ≥3 runs per setting, load quoted per run; report aggregate test
  time as the load-independent metric).
- Confirm memory headroom: RSS per worker tracked; no OOM at the chosen
  setting (the config comment cites memory guardrails as the reason for 4).
- Confirm determinism: 3 consecutive green runs at the chosen setting, no
  intermittent test-timeout or hook-timeout failures.
- Decide and record: either adopt a higher `maxWorkers` (documented) or
  formally keep 4 with the measurement evidence.
