# Pin push-path policy divergence with tests

Test-first safety net for WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push
preamble shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`*).

**No production code changes in this child.** It adds the tests that must be
green **before** `src/sync/push.ts` is refactored, so the dedupe is verified
against pinned behaviour instead of against a re-read of the same code.

## Why

The two push paths deliberately diverge on two policies, and **neither
divergent policy is covered by a test today**:

| Policy | `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) | `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (rewrite) |
|---|---|---|
| Empty stage (`diff --cached` names nothing) | returns silently | throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` |
| Data file missing | returns silently | throws `Worklog data file not found: …` |

Those are exactly the policies a shared helper can silently unify. Each needs a
**negative-proof** test: one that fails if the policy is swapped between the two
paths (an assertion that the other path's behaviour does *not* occur).

Two further divergences must also be pinned byte-exactly:

- the safety-guard message — the incremental path appends
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook.`, the rewrite path
  does not;
- the push flags — `--no-verify` (incremental) vs `--force --no-verify`
  (rewrite).

## Scope — tests only

### `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (incremental path; mock-`git` driven today)

- **Empty stage** resolves without error and performs no push (no `push` call
  in the mock trace / no ref created on the fake remote).
- **Missing data file** (path inside the repo, file absent) resolves without
  error — i.e. it does **not** throw `Worklog data file not found`.
- **`refs/tags/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text, including the
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint.
- **Cross-project guard** still fires when the data file lives in a different
  git repository than the process cwd.
- **Re-point the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion** (currently
  `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts:286-305`): it must keep asserting "no push line
  in `src/sync/push.ts` lacks `--no-verify`" and "a `push --no-verify` line
  exists". Re-pointed, **not deleted or loosened**. The sibling that would
  delete it (WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z) is still at `idea`, so this item owns the
  re-point.

### `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` (rewrite path; real-`git` driven)

- **Empty stage** rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite` — and does
  **not** resolve.
- **`refs/heads/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text and asserts
  the message does **not** carry the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` hint.
- **`--force`** is used: the remote ref is replaced rather than fast-forwarded.
- Keep the existing missing-file, refs-rejection and reentrancy tests unchanged
  in intent.

## Implementation notes

- The mock git (`tests/cli/mock-bin/git`) has **no `diff` handler**: its
  fallback prints the argv to stdout, which makes `diff --cached` look
  non-empty and hides the empty-stage branch. For the incremental empty-stage
  test, prefer a **real-`git`** test in the style of
  `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — seed a bare remote whose
  `refs/worklog/data` already contains byte-identical JSONL, then call
  `gitPushDataFileToBranch` with the same bytes so the copy stages nothing. If
  the mock must gain a `diff` case instead, gate it behind an env var so
  existing suites are unaffected.
- The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup means a seeded ref should
  contain only the data file, or the cleanup will stage deletions.
- Do not weaken an existing assertion to make a new test pass; if a test cannot
  be expressed behaviourally, record an open question rather than grep source.

## Constraints

- No production-code edits (`src/**`).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves without error and performs no push; an added test fails if the incremental path starts throwing.
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`; an added test fails if the rewrite path starts resolving.
  - **Missing data file (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves (no throw) and the rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; each assertion fails if the policies are swapped.
  - **(a) Refs rejection** — `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` rejected on both paths with today's exact text, including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only.
  - **(b) Cross-project guard** — still fires on both paths when the data file belongs to a different git repository.
  - **(e) Push flags** — `--no-verify` on the incremental path; `--force --no-verify` on the rewrite path.

- **Existing suites pass and the grep assertion is not weakened.** `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` pass unchanged in intent; if the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion still exists it is re-pointed (and still asserts the same property) rather than deleted or loosened — if WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z has already replaced it with a behavioural test, no re-point is needed and this clause is satisfied trivially.

Sibling WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z (which would delete it) is still at `idea`.

- **Testing / validation criterion.** The two currently-uncovered policies in AC2(c) and AC2(d) each gain at least one meaningful test that fails if the policy is swapped between the two paths (negative proof, not just a happy-path assertion).

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

- **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
  - `src/sync/push.ts` net shorter; no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
  - `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` unchanged (no re-baselining).
  - `npm run build` green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) green.

- **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
  - Barrel export names and signatures identical; no edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
  - `src/sync/push.ts` module header names the helper and the two mode-specific policies.
  - The `src/sync/push.ts` row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated if the module description changes; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release pipeline owns it).

- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
  - Enforced at the dev-push gate (pre-push hook runs `--scope full`).

## Key Files

- `src/sync/push.ts` — new private helper; both public functions rewritten on
  top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `withTempWorktree`,
  `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`,
  `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` for the
  rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify the exports are identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green);
  `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` must not be regenerated.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the `src/sync/push.ts` row if the module
  description changes.

## Goal

A full-suite run executed from the **main checkout** (e.g. the post-push/audit cache-evidence path) races sibling `implement.py finish` steps: `finish` fast-forwards the main checkout's local `dev` (git merge --ff-only) after pushing, swapping files on disk **while vitest is running**. A suite that starts at commit X but reads files half way through the run can load tests from commit X and source from commit Y (or vice versa), producing unrelated phantom failures. Discovered while verifying WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6.

## Evidence

WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 post-push verification (main checkout, commit 1abe9618): the canonical suite reported 4 failures in `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`, all consistent with new-alphabet tests asserting against old-alphabet behaviour (local-preferred clamped to remote-ok; local-only not clamped). The main checkout reflog shows `merge refs/remotes/origin/dev: Fast-forward` to 2401d874 at exactly that moment (files touched by 2401d874 include packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts, settings.ts, send-to-pi.sh and the failing tests, all with 22:47 mtimes). The exact same tree passed green in an isolated worktree (284 files / 4144 tests) minutes earlier.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Document the race (e.g. in docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md or the implement-skill reference) and/or mitigate it, e.g. run post-push cache-evidence suites against a pinned commit in an isolated worktree and graft the cache entry into the main checkout, instead of running in the live main checkout.
2. The race does not generate additional phantom test-failure items without manual triage.
3. Existing guidance (implement skill post-push verification step) is updated if behaviour changes.

## Problem statement

The per-turn local-preference route log (`<cwd>/.worklog/local-route.log`,
written by `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/` on
`after_provider_response`) is written by interactive panes but **not** by
headless `pi -p` sessions.

## Evidence (verification WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY, 2026-10-29)

- Headless run `01a187e9-2e34-72c3-b1b0-cf42d269c1a0` (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred`,
  `pi -p --model plan`, cwd = a project worktree): the preference header was
  sent (`routing_check … preference=local-preferred` in the proxy log), the
  client retried four 429 deferrals and completed locally, but **no**
  `local-route.log` line was produced in the session cwd.
- Interactive pane `01a18808-a7b1-75ff-b7d0-603be417e6cb` (same env, same
  worktree) wrote the expected line:
  `{"at":"2026-10-29T14:24:01.781Z","sessionId":"01a18808-…","preference":"local-preferred","route":"local","model":"plan"}`.

## Expected

A completed provider response in a headless session should produce the same
bounded route-log entry (the dispatcher's headless background dispatch,
`spawnBackgroundPi`, cannot be audited through the route log today).

## Investigation pointers

- Whether Pi emits `after_provider_response` on the `-p` stream path, and
  whether `event.headers` / `ctx.cwd` are populated there.
  - Verified on this build (plan review, 2026-10-30): the hook is emitted from
    the shared provider-response path (`handleProviderResponse` in
    `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, guarded only by
    `hasHandlers("after_provider_response")`), and the event payload carries
    only `{ type, status, headers }` — `cwd`, `sessionId` and `model` all come
    from the extension `ctx`. The headless gap is therefore most likely a
    `ctx` (cwd/session id) or lifecycle difference on the `-p` path rather
    than a missing emission; confirm before choosing a fix.
- If the hook is not emitted headless, either document the limitation in
  `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  (the reproduction section already carries a HEADLESS CAVEAT note) or capture
  the route from the same transport wrapper the recovery module installs.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` — hook registration (`before_provider_headers`, `after_provider_response`), `ctx.cwd` guard, bounded `appendRouteLogEntry`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` — extension entry point wired through `packages/tui/extensions/package.json` → `pi.extensions`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` — existing pure-module and hook tests (the deterministic coverage AC2 extends these).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.background.ts` — `spawnBackgroundPi` (line ~205), the headless dispatch path whose route evidence is currently missing.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — reproduction/verification section holding the existing "Headless caveat" note.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — extension contract documentation for the route log.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 A headless `pi -p` turn with `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` set either writes
  a route-log entry, or the limitation is documented as intended behaviour.
- AC2 A deterministic test covers the chosen behaviour.
- AC3 Existing route-log tests and the herdr/extension suites stay green.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (to the producer, non-blocking for implementation):** AC1
  offers two resolutions — write the entry headless, or document the
  limitation as intended. `## Expected` above implies the first is preferred
  (a headless dispatch cannot be audited without it), while AC1's second
  branch would be satisfied by the "Headless caveat" note already present in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`. Plan review left AC1 unchanged to avoid
  altering intent; implement should prefer the fix and fall back to
  documenting only if the `-p` path is proven not to carry `ctx` for
  extensions, recording the evidence in the work item. Raise if the
  documentation-only outcome is acceptable as the end state.

# `wl update --status blocked` silently reverts to `open` and still reports success

Discovered while parking `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) on an assignee hold on 2026-10-29.

## Problem

On a specific item, `wl update <id> --status blocked` succeeds, prints `Status ⛔ Blocked`, returns `"status": "blocked"` in `--json`, and then the **stored** record is `open` — with an `updatedAt` 20–30 ms *after* the write that the command reported.

Reproduction (tce-main-street worklog, item `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`):

```
$ wl update MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --status blocked --json | jq -r .workItem.status
blocked
$ sleep 2; wl show MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --json | jq -r '.workItem.status + " " + .workItem.updatedAt'
open 2026-10-29T17:55:59.257Z      # the update's own record said 17:55:59.234Z
```

- Reproduced **4×**, including with `--if-status open`, and via the SQLite store directly (`workitems.status = 'open'`, `updatedAt` = the later timestamp).
- **Not** a sync artefact: `.worklog/last-sync-time` was `17:24:20Z`, well before the writes, and no other `wl` process touched the item (`downtime-*.log`, `local-route.log` checked).
- The revert is specific to **`status`**: `--assignee Map` and `--do-not-delegate true` writes on the same item persist.
- The **create** path persists blocked: sibling items `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO` and `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR` (created with `--status blocked` by the plan) stay blocked.

Distinguishing feature of the affected item: it has **only an inbound** dependency edge (`MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` depends on it) and no outbound edges; its blocking reason is recorded in prose.

## Impact

An explicit status write that silently does not stick is a data-integrity hazard: a caller that blocks an item to stop `wl next` / auto-dispatch from starting it gets `success: true` and a rendered `Blocked` state, but the item stays schedulable. Here it would have allowed a verification child to be started against a prerequisite that has not landed — the exact failure the parent item's Q3 decision is about.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic reproduction exists as a test: create an item, give it an inbound edge only, `wl update --status blocked`, assert the **persisted** status is `blocked` (this currently fails).
- [ ] Root cause named on this item: which write path produces the second record and why it wins (candidates: a post-update re-sort writing from a pre-change snapshot; a derived-status reconciliation that maps blocked-without-outbound-edges to open; a second store/export mirror).
- [ ] Fixed so an explicit `--status blocked` either persists or **fails loudly** with the reason — never `success: true` with a silently different stored value.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the matrix: blocked with no edges; blocked with inbound edges only; blocked with outbound non-terminal edges; blocked with outbound terminal edges; and `--if-status` CAS interaction.
- [ ] The test names are cited on this item as evidence.
- [ ] Full node/pytest suites green for the change.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — status handling, re-sort after update.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` (line ~61 sets `status: 'blocked'` when an edge is added — the semantics the update path should agree with).
- `src/status-stage-rules.ts`, `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` — status/stage compatibility.
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` (`reconcileDependentStatus`) — the second write that reverts the status.
- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`reSort`) — ruled out: writes only `sortIndex`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — SQLite writer used by the store (`worklog.db`); no second mirror.

## Evidence trail

- Origin: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street), comment `MS-C0MVTUG5U90041PQ1` and its follow-up.
- Workaround applied there so the hold is machine-enforced: `--assignee Map` + `do-not-delegate` tag on the affected child.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 (re-run): re-planned an item still at `intake_complete` although its decomposition and root-cause analysis were recorded on 2026-10-29. Verified the root cause against the current tree — `db.update` still calls `hooks.reconcileDependentStatus(id)` after a status/stage change (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`, `updateWorkItem`), that reconciliation still maps `blocked`-with-no-active-blockers to `open` (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`), and `db.update` still returns the pre-reconcile snapshot; `src/commands/update.ts:565` still performs the redundant post-update self-reconcile. Confirmed all cited Key Files exist, except the to-be-created `tests/regression-explicit-blocked-status.test.ts`. Tightened this item's Key Files to real paths (the `src/storage*/` / "worklog.db writer" bullets did not exist). Re-ran the six automated review stages and the AC coverage review (100% coverage by the four children); advanced the stage to `plan_complete`. No children were added, rewritten, or closed.

## Problem

`implement.py finish`'s finish gate runs the suite against a would-be-commit tree using a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2). When the gate falls back to **full scope** (this repo's `.pi/test-config.json` declares custom `suiteCommands`, so changed-scope is never subsettable), the suite's real-git fixtures inherit that `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. A fixture that spreads `process.env` into `spawnSync('git', ...)` therefore stages into the gate's temporary index instead of its own temp repo.

Result observed on WL-0MVTVYNY4001EBRX (ContextHub, 2026-10-30):

```
ERROR: Finish gate: gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran
  (tested tree ae860035..., index now 2b086431...).
  A test staged into the inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE instead of its own repository's index.
```

The gate then aborts (item reset to `open`), and the affected fixtures also fail themselves (`tests/cli/sync-delta-delete.test.ts` `setupProject` git errors). At least ~20 `tests/cli/*.test.ts` files spread `process.env` into git invocations; only fixtures that build a hermetic env are safe.

## Workaround used

Finish was run with `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND='env -u GIT_INDEX_FILE npm --silent test -- tests'`, which still runs the **full** suite at the gate while shielding the non-hermetic fixtures. The gate's index-integrity check then passes. The canonical full suite was also re-run at the pushed commit via `run_tests.py --scope full` for audit evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every test fixture that invokes `git` builds a hermetic environment (drops `GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` unless deliberately testing them) — e.g. a shared TS helper mirroring `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `fixture_git_env()`.
- [ ] A regression test proves a fixture-driven `git add` cannot mutate an inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE`.
- [ ] `implement.py finish` on this repo passes its full-scope gate without the `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND` workaround.

Source: discovered-from WL-0MVTVYNY4001EBRX.

# Remove the heartbeat skill (superseded by the downtime dispatcher)

## Problem statement

The `heartbeat` skill (`/skill:heartbeat`) predates the herdr downtime dispatcher and duplicates — while contradicting — it. It is not in use: no invocation appears anywhere in the Pi session archive, and nothing in `wl`, the herdr plugin, cron, systemd or the test suite calls it. Keeping it costs two drifted copies of the same script that must both be maintained, plus a second, off-contract work-item ranking path.

## Evidence gathered (2026-10-30)

**No usage:**

- `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: zero occurrences of `/skill:heartbeat` as a user prompt (`"text":"/skill:heartbeat"` → 0 files); the ~1,000 hits are the skill-catalogue description embedded in every system prompt.
- No tool-result output of a real run (`"Flagged … for producer review"`, `"No items in completed/in_review queue"`) anywhere in the archive — those strings appear only inside the skill's own source/SKILL.md text.
- No crontab entry, no systemd timer, no herdr plugin hook, no caller in `packages/herdr/src` (the only "heartbeat" hits there are the unrelated *sync* heartbeat), no reference from any other skill.

**Superseded by the downtime dispatcher** (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`):

| | `heartbeat` skill | Downtime dispatcher |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | manual `/skill:heartbeat`, one action per call | continuous, leader-elected idle dispatch |
| Audit invocation | headless `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`, 600 s timeout, invisible | visible herdr pane, with pane monitor, stall resume and attempt budget |
| Audit threshold | review queue ≥ 10 (hard-coded) | review-queue gate `count >= browseItemCount` (live setting) + depth-aware audit batching |
| Candidate ranking | `wl next` — a **second ranking path** | "dispatcher == Herdr list head"; a second ranking is explicitly disallowed |
| `needsProducerReview` | set as a "look at this next" nudge on a sparse queue | a **dispatch hold**, set only on attempt-budget exhaustion |

**Duplicate drift:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` (resolved at runtime) and `skill/heartbeat/` (imported by the tests) are separate git-tracked copies that have diverged in their audit dispatch (`pi -p` vs `audit_runner.py`); the parity guard in `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` exists only to stop further divergence. Removal eliminates the drift by construction.

**Deliberate coverage loss:** automated audit dispatch without herdr. The dispatcher lives in the herdr plugin and requires idle local-LLM capacity; a herdr-less mode would need a new implementation against the dispatcher's contract. Accepted — there is no herdr-less deployment today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/heartbeat/` and `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` are removed from the repository, so `/skill:heartbeat` no longer resolves in Pi and no duplicate copy remains.
2. `tests/skill/heartbeat/` (unit and integration suites) is removed; no test imports or references the heartbeat module.
3. The `README.md` feature blurb and the docs table row advertising the heartbeat skill are removed.
4. Stale prose is corrected: `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` no longer lists heartbeat as a `wl` consumer (inventory table and both summary rows), and `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` no longer refers to "heartbeat tooling" as a queue consumer.
5. The superseded work items recorded as deleted with the dispatcher named as the replacement: heartbeat audit notifications (WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI) and the `.pi` copy-drift item (WL-0MVVM0SLV0053QP8). *(Both were soft-deleted at filing time; this AC needs no implementation work — verify only that nothing still references them.)*
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (CHANGELOG.md is release-managed and excluded).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/heartbeat/` — delete (SKILL.md, `scripts/heartbeat.py`, `__init__.py`).
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` — delete (runtime copy).
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py`, `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat_integration.py` — delete alongside the skill.
- `README.md` — remove the feature blurb (~line 11) and the docs table row (~line 140).
- `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — drop heartbeat from the `wl`-consumer inventory and per-invocation rows.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — reword the "heartbeat/release tooling" reference (~line 74).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — remove the heartbeat entry from the known skill-behaviour-drift note (~line 735) if it becomes stale.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher is the sole replacement for background audit dispatch; no herdr-less automation exists to preserve.
- **Assumption:** the "ready for producer review prior to a new release" report has no unique consumer (the ship/release gate and worklist header cover it); if that changes, it belongs in the worklist header, not a standalone skill.
- **Risk — muscle memory:** a user typing `/skill:heartbeat` will now get "skill not found" rather than a silent no-op. Accepted; the failure is loud and harmless.
- **Risk — stale references:** prose in `docs/dev/` and the README mentions the skill in several places; AC4 covers the substantive ones and a repo-wide grep for `heartbeat` (excluding the unrelated sync heartbeat and `CHANGELOG.md`) should come back clean.
- **Scope creep guard:** do not port heartbeat's sparse-queue nudge into the dispatcher — `wl reviewed <id> true` plus the TUI icon already cover manual producer flagging.

## Related work

- `Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)` — the original item, now superseded.
- `Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7)` — documents the headless-visibility gap that led here.
- `Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (WL-0MSACL482002RNYH)` — the toast plumbing the (withdrawn) notification proposal would have reused.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the replacement mechanism.

# Intake Brief: hydrator must not demote `in-progress` claims held by pane-less driven sessions

Created from `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK` (llm store) per producer decision Q1 = **B**: the defect record lives here now; the reporting item was deleted after this item was created and synced.

## Problem statement

`decideDemotion()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:497`) treats *"no pane title in this workspace contains the item ID"* as *"nobody is working this item"* and releases the claim (`in-progress/* → open/intake_complete`, or `blocked` / `completed` on the other branches) on every 30 s cycle. A **driven child session** — `implement.py drive` → `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>"` — is headless by design (`WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7`) and therefore can never produce a matching pane, so every claim it makes is reverted within one cycle while it is still editing. The same single-signal rule also releases items whose herdr pane title no longer contains the ID.

## Users

- **Driven/headless implement sessions** (`implement.py drive` / `phase` / `start`) — as a driven session, my `in_progress` claim must survive while my process is alive, so `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` does not fail mid-work and no second session is handed the same item.
- **Producer / operator** — as a producer, `in_progress` must mean "someone is actually working this", *and* abandoned claims must still self-heal without manual intervention.
- **Dispatching agents** (`wl next`, the downtime worker) — as a dispatcher, I must never receive an item a live session is editing (the duplicate-dispatch failure `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` exists to prevent).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Live claim holder suppresses demotion.** An item that is `in-progress` with **no** matching pane but whose `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is currently **held** (non-blocking `flock` fails with `EWOULDBLOCK`) is left untouched by the cycle. Covered by a unit test that takes a real flock in the test process.
2. **Dead holders are still released (no regression to stuck claims).** An item with a lock file whose `flock` is free **and** whose recorded `pid` is not alive is demoted exactly as today (`open`/`intake_complete`), within one cycle — covered by a unit test using a stale fixture lock.
3. **Existing decision branches are unchanged.** Pane match ⇒ untouched; no lock file ⇒ demoted; active outbound dep blocker ⇒ `blocked`; stage `in_review` ⇒ `completed`; a held claim never overrides the `blocked`/`in_review` branches — all covered by tests.
4. **Fail-open on ambiguity.** An unreadable lock directory, a malformed/corrupt lock file, or an unexpected `fs`/`flock` error **suppresses demotion** and logs a named reason (mirroring the existing `wl`/`herdr` fail-open), rather than releasing the claim — covered by a test per error class.
5. **Pid-reuse guard.** The `pid` fallback is only trusted when the lock's `started_at` is not earlier than the recorded process start time; otherwise the probe reports *held* (fail-open) and names the reason in the log, so a recycled pid can never be read as a live claim — covered by a test with a fabricated stale `started_at`.
6. **Cost stays bounded.** The lock directory is read **once per cycle**, with no additional `wl`/`herdr` spawns per item and no wall-clock TTL/heartbeat; a test asserts the spawn and directory-read counts for a multi-item cycle.
7. **Release clears the scheduling hold (Q3 = A).** When the hydrator releases a claim it also clears `assignee` (`wl update … --assignee ""`) and records the previous holder in the release audit comment (e.g. `released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: implement`). A test asserts the `wl update` argument vector and the comment body; live verification: after a release, `wl show <id>` reports an empty `assignee` and the release comment names the previous holder.
8. **Diagnosable log lines.** Every suppression and every release names the deciding signal, e.g. `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` and `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)` — existing hydrator log-format tests extended.
9. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` (Design step 3 + Safety list) and the `hydrator.ts` module header describe the second signal, its fail-open rules, the pid-reuse guard, the `assignee`-clearing behaviour, and the explicit non-goal (no TTL / no heartbeat).
10. **Producer directive reconciled.** The docs restate and keep the producer's rule — "It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`, quoted at `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md:58`) — as the **primary** signal, with the claim holder added as a second, mechanically verifiable signal for pane-less sessions.
11. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
12. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm run build` + `npm test` in the repository root).

## Constraints

- **Keep the pane rule primary.** Pane-title matching was chosen after the producer rejected tab-label matching as unreliable (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`); add to it, do not replace it.
- **No new protocol, no TTL.** The claim signal is the existing per-child lock produced by `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` (installed from SorraAgents). It is **kernel-authoritative while held** and its file **persists after release**, so existence and `started_at` age are never liveness evidence — only `flock` heldness (with the guarded `pid` fallback) is.
  - Measured 2026-10-31 on the llm store: 40 `child-*.lock` files, **all** recording pids that were no longer alive. An existence check would suppress demotion forever.
- **Read the lock contract defensively.** `{agent, pid, session_id, started_at, token}` is a diagnostic sidecar; unknown or extra fields must not break the probe, and `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy means a holder chain (driver → `parent`/`start` subprocess → driven child) may present the same token.
- **Budget.** A cycle already races a 5 s per-step budget inside a 20 s run watchdog (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` / `HYDRATOR_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ`); the probe must be local `fs` I/O only, resolved from the worklog root already available via `getWorklogDir()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- **Fail-open asymmetry is deliberate.** Ambiguity ⇒ no demotion; affirmative death ⇒ release.
- **Scope.** Do not redesign dispatch, the worklist selection marker, the drive orchestrator, or `implement.py`. Adjacent opportunities (hydrator log rotation, orphaned-lock cleanup) are separate items.

## Evidence (captured from the reporting store before its log rotated)

`.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` in `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`, window 2026-10-31T04:10–04:37Z — ten releases, three items, all `in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no matching pane)`:

| Time (UTC) | Item | Releases | State after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 04:10:59, 04:11:29, 04:28:30 | `LP-0MVT1NVAJ007KUGO` | 3 | later `blocked/intake_complete` |
| 04:14:59, 04:15:29, 04:31:00, 04:31:30, 04:32:00, 04:36:31 | `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` | 6 | `open/intake_complete`, `assignee=Map` (stale hold — AC7) |
| 04:29:30 | `LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12` | 1 | completed in_review by its own session |

Earlier evidence (2026-10-30T20:49–20:52Z, `LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO`, three releases interleaved with the live session's writes) had already rotated out: `hydrator.log` keeps only the live ~200-line window with no archive. Also unverified and therefore recorded as *reported, not reproduced*: a release of `LP-0MVSAM2AV0077UAE` attributed to a herdr pane whose id changed.

## Desired change

A cycle decides "busy" from two independent signals and demotes only when both are negative:

1. **Pane signal (unchanged, primary)** — a pane in the current workspace whose title contains the item ID ⇒ busy.
2. **Claim-holder signal (new)** — a **live** claim holder for the item: `child-<id>.lock` currently flocked, or the guarded pid fallback ⇒ busy.

## Fix specification

1. **Extend the injected deps** with `hasLiveClaimHolder(itemIds): Promise<Map<string, boolean>>` (batch over the cycle's candidate list) alongside the existing `HydratorDeps` seams, so orchestration stays unit-testable with no real filesystem.
2. **Decision input.** Add `held` to the `decideDemotion()` context and return `null` when `ctx.hasActivePane || ctx.held`; keep the `blocked` / `in_review` ordering untouched.
3. **Probe.** Resolve the worklog root once per cycle, enumerate `locks/child-*.lock` once, then per candidate: non-blocking `flock` (acquire succeeds ⇒ release immediately and fall back to guarded `pid` liveness; `EWOULDBLOCK` ⇒ held; missing file ⇒ not held; any other error ⇒ held + named log reason).
4. **Release path.** Pass `--assignee ""` on the demotion `wl update` and append the previous holder to the audit comment (Q3 = A).
5. **Tests** in `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — one per AC 1–8, using a temp worklog root with real `flock` fixtures.
6. **Docs** — `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` and the module header (ACs 9–10).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `decideDemotion()` (line 497), the orchestration cycle (`runHydrationOnce`), `HydratorDeps` (line ~246), `createProductionHydratorDeps().applyDemotion` (line 1030): add the claim-holder signal, the heldness probe, and `--assignee ""`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new decision, probe and orchestration cases (1,348 lines today).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` / `buildWlArgs()` already resolve the store root the probe needs.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — Design step 3 + Safety list + Files section.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` — lock contract being read (read-only; `agent`/`pid`/`session_id`/`started_at`/`token`, `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy).
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the holder population (`_new_child_lock` / `_set_child_lock`, ~lines 696–760); read-only.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI` (completed) — *Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane*: introduced this demotion rule and `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` (completed) — the producer's pane-title directive and the selection-list marker.
- `WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US` (completed) — *Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items*: AC3 defines the `open`/`intake_complete` release target.
- `WL-0MTTSWE0G008M1VA` (deleted, folded into `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`) — the "no pane ⇒ stale regardless of age" claim-age rule this item qualifies.
- `WL-0MTWU4Y82001B3UH` (completed) — demotion must leave an audit-trail comment (extended by AC7).
- `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ`, `WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO`, `WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX` (completed) — per-step budgets, stdio isolation and bounded ticks constraining the probe.
- `WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI` (completed) — hydrator docs/pane-title rationale, the doc to update.
- `WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7` (completed) — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless `pi -p` vs herdr pane*: why driven sessions have no pane.
- `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` — *actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`* invariant (SorraAgents store), the contract this violates.
- `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` — per-child lock rationale (`drive` duplicate-session RCA).
- `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK` (llm store) — the defect report this item was created from (deleted after this item was created and synced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pid reuse.** A stale lock whose pid now belongs to an unrelated process would suppress demotion indefinitely. Mitigation: `flock` is authoritative; the pid fallback is gated on `started_at` (AC5) and logged.
- **Risk — cross-repo coupling.** The hydrator would depend on a lock format owned by the globally installed skills. Mitigation: defensively parse (unknown ⇒ fail-open), document the contract in `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, and keep the probe behind an injected seam so the source can change without touching orchestration.
- **Risk — re-introducing stuck claims.** Any suppression that outlives the holder re-creates `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`'s original defect. Mitigation: no TTL, kernel liveness only, AC2 test.
- **Risk — cost creep per tick.** A per-item filesystem probe over a large in-progress list. Mitigation: one directory read per cycle, map lookup per item (AC6).
- **Assumption.** The `implement.py` lock is held for the whole driven-session lifetime (`phase_start` through session exit), so it is a faithful "session is alive" proxy — verified in `implement.py` (`_set_child_lock` / `_release_child_lock`, released in the phase cleanup and by the kernel on crash).
- **Assumption.** A pane-less session may still be *pane-visible* if a wrapper later spawns one; the change is a strict superset of the current signal, so no existing behaviour is narrowed.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Log rotation, orphaned-lock cleanup, drive-orchestrator changes: separate items, not scope here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 "Should the fix be raised as a work item in this store, with the llm report item deleted once created and synced?"** — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-31): B — "b, once created and synced delete this item"**: create the implementation item here, sync, then delete `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK`. Source: producer reply on `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK`; evidence: this item's creation, the sync in this store, and the deletion reason on the reporting item.
- **Q2 "Which pane-less claim signal should the hydrator honour?"** — **Answer (producer): A** — the existing per-child lock `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, probed for *heldness* via non-blocking `flock` with a guarded pid-liveness fallback. Research: `work_item_lock.py` (kernel releases the flock on exit/SIGKILL; metadata is diagnostic only); 40/40 existing lock files on the llm store recorded dead pids, so heldness — never existence — is the signal.
- **Q3 "When the hydrator releases a claim, should it also clear `assignee`?"** — **Answer (producer): A** — clear it and record the previous holder in the release audit comment; a released item must not stay parked on a scheduling hold (live example: `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` was `open/intake_complete` with `assignee=Map` after its 04:36:31Z release, because `applyDemotion` passes only `--status`/`--stage`).

## Summary

Implement the single core project-discovery scan and expose it as
`wl project list` — one implementation for the whole framework (D1, D6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cross-repo/project-registry.ts` exposes `discoverProjects({ projectsRoot?, cwd? })`
  returning `{ projectsRoot, projects: [{ prefix, path, ambiguous? }] }`, memoised
  per process, with exactly one `readdir` of the projects root plus two
  `existsSync` probes per candidate — no repository-wide walk. The bound is
  asserted by spying on `fs.readdirSync`/`fs.existsSync` call counts in the
  discovery test, not merely claimed.
- Genuine-store discrimination reuses `isGenuineWorklogStore()` from
  `src/worklog-paths.ts` (`initialized` or `worklog.db`); no duplicated probe
  logic. Non-git folders, hidden folders and managed worktrees are excluded.
- `wl project list [--json]` prints the `prefix → path` map sorted by prefix;
  `--json` shape is `{ success, projectsRoot, projects: [{ prefix, path, ambiguous }] }`.
- `projectsRoot` is read from `.worklog/config.yaml` (key `projectsRoot`),
  defaulting to the parent directory of the current checkout, and is documented
  in `./CONFIG.md`.
- The command is registered in `src/command-registry.ts` (including
  `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`) and appears in the `wl --help` grouping.
- The F1 discovery spec passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/cross-repo/project-registry.ts` — scan, memoise, ambiguity detection,
  projects-root resolution.
- `src/config.ts` — `projectsRoot` (and the `projects` map placeholder) in
  `WorklogConfig`.
- `src/commands/project.ts` — `project list` subcommand.
- `src/command-registry.ts` + `src/cli-main.ts` help grouping.
- `./CONFIG.md`, `./CLI.md` — `projectsRoot` and `wl project list`.

## Dependencies

Cross-repo fixture harness and discovery spec.

## Deliverables

- Discovery module, `wl project list`, config key, help/docs entry.

**Key Files:**

- `src/cross-repo/project-registry.ts` — **new** discovery module
- `src/commands/project.ts` — **new** `project list`
- `src/config.ts` — `projectsRoot` config key
- `src/command-registry.ts` — lazy loader + built-in name
- `./CONFIG.md`, `./CLI.md` — documentation

## Summary

Write the failing specification for foreign dependency edges (AC2) and the
read-only guarantee (AC5): recording and reading a foreign edge must never
write to, lock or sync the sibling store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/cross-repo-dep-edges.test.ts` asserts `wl dep add <local-id> <foreign-id>`
  succeeds and `dep list` shows the foreign item's title and status (red until F4).
- The local dependent is set to `blocked` and the edge survives a re-read of the
  local database.
- The sibling store's `worklog.db` **content hash and mtime** are unchanged after
  the foreign edge is added, listed and evaluated, and no `-wal`, `-shm` or lock
  file is created in the sibling `.worklog/` directory (read-only proof, AC5).
- `wl dep rm <local-id> <foreign-id>` removes the edge and reconciles the
  dependent back to `open`.
- Same-project `dep add` / `dep rm` / `dep list` human and `--json` output is
  byte-identical to a recorded baseline (regression, AC2).

## Minimal Implementation

## Summary

Record foreign dependency edges in the local store while resolving the foreign
endpoint strictly read-only (D2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC traceability.** **AC2 — Foreign edge recorded, foreign store untouched.** `wl dep add` with a foreign id succeeds, the edge is listed by `dep list` with the foreign title and status, the local dependent is set to `blocked`, and the sibling DB's file (content hash and mtime) is unchanged. Same-project `dep add`/`rm`/`list` output is byte-identical to today (regression).
- `wl dep add` accepts an id whose prefix belongs to a discovered sibling store:
  existence is validated against that store, and the edge is written to the
  **local** store with the foreign id as `toId`.
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` gains an explicit
  foreign-target path (e.g. `addDependencyEdge(ctx, from, to, { allowForeignTarget: true })`)
  so the existing local-endpoint invariant is unchanged for same-project calls.
- `wl dep rm <local-id> <foreign-id>` removes the edge and reconciles the
  dependent, with no write to the foreign store.
- A prefix declared by two discovered projects is refused as **ambiguous** with
  both candidate paths in the error — never silently resolved to one of them.
- `wl dep list --json` includes foreign entries carrying `title`, `status`,
  `stage`, `foreign: true` and `foreign_dependency: "resolved" | "unresolved" | "unavailable"`.
- The sibling store is opened read-only (`readonly: true`, `fileMustExist: true`)
  with no mutation lock, no sync and no WAL write; a missing or unreadable store
  degrades to `unavailable` instead of throwing.
- `wl dep --help` states that foreign (cross-project) ids are supported.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` — read-only open, `getForeignItem(id)`,
  tri-state resolution result, no writes.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — foreign branch for `add`, `rm`, `list`; foreign
  metadata in `--json` and human output.
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — `allowForeignTarget` option.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — helper to decide "is this id local, foreign-resolvable or unknown".
- The F3 spec passes.

## Dependencies

Foreign dependency edge and isolation spec.

## Deliverables

- Read-only foreign store resolver.
- Foreign edge CRUD in `wl dep`.
- `dep --help` update.

**Key Files:**

- `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` — **new** read-only resolver
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — foreign branch for add/rm/list
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — local/foreign/unknown id classification
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — `allowForeignTarget`

## Summary

Make every dependency-blocker evaluation resolve foreign targets from their own
store, with an explicit fail-safe when the store is unavailable (D3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC traceability.** **AC3 — Gating.** An item whose only active blocker is a foreign item is excluded from `wl next` and included with `--include-blocked`; the same item becomes selectable once the foreign item reaches `in_review`/`done`/ `completed`/`deleted`; a removed sibling store leaves the item blocked with `unresolved: true` and a reason in JSON (never unblocked).
- `getActiveDependencyBlockers`, `hasActiveBlockers` and every `isDependencyActive`
  consumer resolve a foreign target's `status`/`stage` from its own store using
  the existing terminal semantics — the predicate is reused, not forked.
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` `buildEdgeCache` keeps foreign targets
  out of `itemsById`, and no resolver assumes a local row exists.
- `wl next` blocked-candidate filtering, `--include-blocked` and blocker surfacing
  (`next-pipeline.ts`) report foreign blockers with `unresolved` and a `reason`.
- `wl doctor` distinguishes an unresolved foreign edge (`severity: warning`,
  `foreign_dependency: unresolved`) from a genuinely missing local endpoint
  (the existing `dependency.missing-endpoint` error) — no false finding.
- Fail-safe: a foreign store that disappears mid-run leaves the dependent
  blocked and logs one warning; no unhandled exception, no silent unblock.
- An **ambiguous** foreign prefix is never resolved to one candidate: the blocker
  is reported `unresolved: true` with an `ambiguous` reason and stays blocking.
- The F5 gating spec passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — foreign resolution + fail-safe
  in `isDependencyActive`/`getActiveDependencyBlockers`/`hasActiveBlockers`.
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` — edge cache stays local-only.
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — surface unresolved blockers.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` + `src/doctor/dependency-check.ts` — foreign-aware check.
- `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` — resolution cache for the gating hot path.

## Dependencies

Foreign blocker gating and fail-safe spec.

## Deliverables

- Foreign-aware blocker resolution across `next`, `worklist`, `list`, `doctor`
  and `dep list`.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — foreign resolution + fail-safe
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` — `buildEdgeCache` stays local-only
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — unresolved blocker surfacing
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/doctor/dependency-check.ts` — foreign-aware check

## Summary

Implement `wl project add` (URL + clone + config mapping) and the
`unknown_project` error surface that replaces the bare `Work item not found`
(D4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC traceability.** **AC4 — Missing project remediation.** An unknown prefix produces `error_code: "unknown_project"` with the projects root and the exact `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url>` remediation; `wl project add` clones into the projects root, records the mapping, validates the prefix, and is idempotent; a prefix mismatch or clone failure exits non-zero without leaving a mapping behind; no stdin prompt without `--interactive`.
- `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <dir>]` records
  `projects.<PREFIX>.path` (and the git URL) in `.worklog/config.yaml`, cloning
  with `git clone <url> <path>` only when the path does not exist.
- The cloned store's `config.yaml` prefix must match `PREFIX`; a mismatch exits
  non-zero with remediation and writes no mapping.
- A clone failure exits non-zero, leaves no mapping and no partial directory
  behind in the projects root.
- Re-running against an existing correct clone is a no-op (no clone, no duplicate
  mapping, exit 0).
- No stdin prompt by default; `--interactive` prompts for the URL only when
  `--git-url` is omitted. Git credentials come from the operator's existing git
  configuration — the tool never prompts for them.
- `wl dep add`, `wl dep list` and `wl next` return the `unknown_project` payload
  (`prefix`, `projects_root`, `remediation`) instead of a bare
  `Work item not found`.
- The F7 spec passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/commands/project.ts` — `project add` subcommand, `--git-url`, `--path`,
  `--interactive`.

data.description:
Discovered while diagnosing local/remote routing for LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C on
2026-10-31 (proxy-log-debug session). Proxy-side sibling defect is filed
separately in the llm store (see Related work).

## Summary

The downtime worker's local-capacity reservation client posts
`expected_tokens`, but `POST /llama/local/reserve` requires
`estimated_tokens`. The proxy answers `400 {"error":"estimated_tokens is
required"}`, `createLocalReserver` maps any non-2xx/non-429 response to `null`
(fail-open by design), and the dispatcher therefore launches the pane with **no
ticket and no capacity check**. The only dispatch-time local-capacity gate in the
worker is inert, and it fails silently — a dispatch record shows
`reservationTicketId: null, reservation: null` with no deferral reason.

## Problem statement

`buildLocalReservationRequest` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts:117-125`)
returns:

```ts
{ expected_tokens: DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS /* 8192 */,
  priority: 'background', cache_state: 'unknown' }
```

The proxy's handler (`proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:396-410`) reads only
`estimated_tokens`:

```python
raw_tokens = body.get("estimated_tokens")
if raw_tokens is None:
    return 400, {"error": "estimated_tokens is required", "admit": False}
```

Verified live against the running proxy (2026-10-31, read-only `dry_run`):

```
POST /llama/local/reserve {"expected_tokens":4000,…}
  → 400 {"error": "estimated_tokens is required", "admit": false}
POST /llama/local/reserve {"estimated_tokens":4000,…}
  → 200 {"admit": true, "dry_run": true, "reason": "within_budget",
          "projected_wait_s": 7.8, "budget_s": 60.0}
```

Consequence: `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts:295-330` documents
"refused (429) → DEFER with the proxy's retry_after_s, roll the claim back",
but an unusable *request* can never produce a refusal — only `null`, which the
code treats as "older proxy, fail open, dispatch anyway". The per-dispatch
capacity handshake (parent WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8, slice C2) is therefore dead
code in production, and the worker cannot distinguish "proxy too old" from
"our body is wrong".

Evidence from the live dispatch that exposed it
(`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, llm project, 2026-10-31T12:49:27Z):

```json
{ "itemId": "LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C", "kind": "audit",
  "localPreference": "remote-ok", "localPreferenceReason": "default",
  "reservationTicketId": null, "reservation": null }
```

## Users

- **Primary user — the operator.** Believes dispatched work is admitted against
  real local capacity; in fact nothing is checked, so a burst of downtime panes
  can pile onto a 2-slot local pool (or, as on 2026-10-31, be launched
  `remote-ok` while nobody notices the gate never ran).
- **Secondary user — the next maintainer of the reservation handshake.** A
  silent 400/no-ticket loop makes the feature look "fail-open working" instead
  of "contract broken".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The request body the client builds uses the field the proxy contract
      requires (`estimated_tokens`) and a unit test pins the exact wire body
      against the documented proxy contract, so a rename on either side fails
      the test rather than degrading to `null`.
- [ ] A `429` refusal still defers the dispatch with the proxy's
      `retry_after_s`, rolls the claim back, and writes no success marker /
      spawn (existing C2 behaviour retained, asserted by test).
- [ ] Fail-open is preserved for genuinely unusable responses (`404`, `5xx`,
      timeout, unparseable body) — asserted by the existing tests, unchanged.
- [ ] An unusable-response outcome is **distinguishable from a refusal** in the
      dispatch record/log (e.g. a `reservationUnavailable`/probe-failure field
      or a log line naming the failing exchange), so a broken contract can never
      again look like an old proxy.
- [ ] End-to-end evidence recorded on this item: after the fix, a real downtime
      dispatch on this host records a non-null `reservationTicketId` when the
      proxy grants, and a deferral reason when it refuses (capture the
      `downtime-dispatches.log` entry in a comment).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes
      (`packages/herdr` suite plus the repo-wide suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the handshake fail-open: an older/absent proxy must still never block a
  dispatch.
- Do not change the pane locality policy (`remote-ok` default, `low`-priority
  rule) — that is deliberate and out of scope.
- No proxy changes in this repo; the proxy owns its own contract (sibling item).
- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is already dirty in this checkout from
  unrelated work — leave it alone.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts` — request builder
  (`buildLocalReservationRequest:117`) and the tolerant parser/client
  (`createLocalReserver`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `LocalReservationRequest`
  (`expected_tokens` at ~376).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — the reserve gate
  (~295–330) and the dispatch record fields.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` —
  `DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS` / `LOCAL_RESERVE_PATH`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` and the
  dispatch-claims tests — where the wire-body assertion and the
  refuse/rollback cases belong.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-31)

- `downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts:110` — `DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS = 8_192`;
  `:121` — `expected_tokens: DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS`.
- `downtime-worker.types.ts:376` — `expected_tokens: number;`.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:398` — proxy requires `estimated_tokens`
  (introduced by LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL on the proxy side).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1474` — `downtimeDeps.reserveLocalCapacity = createLocalReserver(runSettings.downtimeProxyUrl);`
  so the client IS wired; only the wire body is wrong.
- No existing work item covers this: `wl search "reservation ticket
  expected_tokens mismatch"` → 0 results in the llm store; no matching item in
  this store either.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` — parent: atomic local-admission reservation handshake
  (slices C1/C2/C3).
- `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (llm store) — proxy side of the handshake; defines
  `estimated_tokens` and the 429 refusal contract.
- `WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX` / `WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1` — pane locality preference
  (`remote-ok` default), the reason this defect stayed invisible: panes go
  remote anyway, so nobody missed the missing ticket.
- llm-store sibling item — "measured-cache-deficit 503 quarantines the whole
  local entry", the other defect found in the same diagnosis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — other clients of `/llama/local/reserve`.** Check for a second caller
  (e.g. the pi Worklog extension) before changing only this one; the fix should
  make the wire contract single-sourced if more than one caller exists.
- **Risk — proxy-side tolerance masking it again.** If the proxy ever accepts
  `expected_tokens` as an alias, this bug becomes invisible again; the
  acceptance evidence in AC5 pins the behaviour end-to-end instead of relying on
  reading code.
- **Assumption.** The proxy's `estimated_tokens` name is the intended contract
  (documented in `admission_reserve.py` and exercised by the live 200/400
  responses). If the proxy side is judged the one to change, coordinate with the
  sibling llm item rather than diverging.

## Review update (2026-10-31, follow-up diagnosis)

The wire-body mismatch is confirmed, and a second independent gap was found while
tracing the same window: **even with the body fixed, the ticket cannot protect the
local capacity this dispatch actually needs.**

Facts established from the proxy log and the code:

- Ticket TTL is `DEFAULT_RESERVE_TTL_SECONDS = 10` (max 60)
  (`llm/proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:52-53`), and the ticket reaches only the
  **pane** process via `PI_LOCAL_RESERVATION_TICKET` — the extension at
  `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts:63` is what turns it
  into the `X-Local-Reservation` header.
- A downtime audit dispatch runs its own agent loop with
  `localPreference: remote-ok` (medium priority ⇒ `default`), so its first request
  goes **remote** and the granted ticket is never consumed — the proxy already tracks
  these as reserved-but-unused (`admission_reserve.py` `stats()`:
  `reserved_issued` / `reserved_used` / `reserved_expired`, exposed through the
  `/llama/local/status` payload at `proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1054`).
- The process that *does* need local capacity is the audit runner's own `pi`
  subprocess (`audit-LP-…-parent-…`, `prefer-local`). It starts ~12 minutes after the
  dispatch and runs `pi --no-context-files --no-skills --no-extensions`
  (`audit_runner.py:4593`), so it cannot send `X-Local-Reservation` even though it
  inherits the env var — and the 10 s TTL expired long before.
- Observed consequence in the same window: dispatch `12:28:50` (proxy reported
  `available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle`); the audit's first local attempt at
  `12:40:05` succeeded once, then `12:41:13 local_dispatch_denied` (slot owned by
  another session) → `fallback_after_queue` → remote. Final tally for that audit
  subprocess: **1 local / 7 remote streams**.

So fixing AC1 alone would leave the dispatch record looking healthy
(`reservationTicketId` non-null, AC5 evidence green) while local utilisation stays
near zero — the "green but unmet" outcome this item exists to prevent.

### Additional acceptance criteria (from the review)

- [ ] **AC7 — The reservation must have a real beneficiary.** Assert end-to-end that
      a granted ticket is consumed by the request it was granted for (proxy
      `/llama/local/status` reservation counters show `reserved_used ≥ 1` and
      `reserved_outstanding` returns to 0 for the dispatch), **or** that no ticket is
      requested when the dispatched session cannot consume local capacity. The chosen
      rule is documented on this item with its rationale and pinned by a test.
- [ ] **AC8 — No reserved-but-unused tickets for downtime panes.** A `remote-ok`
      dispatch (the default for every non-`low` priority candidate,
      `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`) must not reserve local capacity it will never use:
      either skip the reserve call for such dispatches and record that decision in the
      dispatch record, or reserve for the process that will consume it. A dispatch
      record must never show both `reservationTicketId != null` and a session that
      issues no local request.
- [ ] **AC9 — Bound and document the TTL / beneficiary limitation.** Record on this
      item and in `downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`'s docstring that the ticket
      TTL is 10 s and that only the pane's own first request can consume it; if a
      local-consuming child process (audit runner, or any `--no-extensions` session)
      is ever expected to use a ticket, either raise the TTL for that path or have the
      child take its own reservation — silently relying on an expired ticket is not
      acceptable. Asserted by a test that a ticket older than the TTL is not treated
      as capacity by the client.

## Review update #2 (2026-10-31, proxy-log review — llm session `herdr-1793450762-1330301-22426`)

### Independent confirmation from the proxy side

- The dispatch record for the audit in the reviewed window shows exactly the state this
  item describes: `localPreference: "remote-ok"`, `localPreferenceReason: "default"`,
  `reservationTicketId: null`, `reservation: null` — and **no** deferral/unavailable
  marker, so the record cannot tell "policy" from "broken client".
- The proxy side of the pair is confirmed too: `/llama/local/status` reported
  `available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle llama_server_running=true` for the whole
  pre-dispatch window (12:44–12:46), and the dispatched audit nevertheless ran
  **45/45 requests and 37/37 streams remote** — because the local entry was in a
  repeating 60 s cooldown armed by another session's measured-cache aborts
  (llm-store sibling LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ, AC1/AC10/AC11 now cover the proxy fix).
- So the two defects compose exactly as the "Review update" says: the wire-body fix
  (AC1) would have produced a *successful* reservation for a local capacity this
  dispatch could never use, and the ticket counters would have looked healthy.

### The trap in AC7/AC8 option (a) — record it before implementing

AC8 permits "skip the reserve call for `remote-ok` dispatches and record that decision".
Taken **alone**, that makes *no ticket* the documented norm for every non-`low` priority
candidate, and the ticket disappears as a health signal entirely: a dispatch record that
never had a ticket looks identical whether the run used 100 % local or 100 % remote. The
operator's real question ("did my unattended work actually use the GPU I paid for?") then
has no answer in this repo. Hence AC10 — it is the outcome-level counterpart to the
proxy-side status fields, and it is what makes option (a) safe.

### Additional acceptance criterion

- [ ] **AC10 — record the observed routing outcome, so a green dispatch record cannot
      hide a 0 %-local run.** Every dispatch record (or the same `downtime-dispatches`
      entry, written when the pane's work window closes) carries the **observed** split
      for the dispatched session: `localStreams` and `remoteStreams` (or an equivalent
      `localShare`), sourced from the bounded route log / proxy session attribution —
      never from the reservation ticket. A dispatch whose session issued requests and
      consumed **0 local** capacity is recorded with an explicit `localStarved: true`,
      and when the dispatched work is `prefer-local` (e.g. an audit whose runner
      subprocess is `prefer-local`) a WARNING line names the dispatch, the split and the
      proxy's `local_route_reason` if available. Tests: a stub route log producing
      0 local / 7 remote yields `localStarved: true` with the split recorded; a
      mixed 3/4 split yields `localStarved: false`; a dispatch with no requests at all
      is recorded as `notObserved` (never as healthy). Rationale: AC7/AC8 may legitimately
      remove the ticket — the observed outcome must take over as the capacity-health
      signal, otherwise this item's own "end-to-end evidence" (AC5) can pass while local
      utilisation is ~0, which is the failure mode that motivated the review update.

### Planning note for whoever picks this up

AC10 was added after `plan_complete`; the plan's task breakdown needs one line for it
(record the outcome from the route log at window close + the stub-log tests). No other
AC changes: AC1–AC9 stand as written.
